# Introduction

In today’s lecture, we will examine:

- **Outliers**: Where are the data located?
- **Dispersion**: How spread out are the data?
- **Shape**: What does the distribution look like?
- **Bivariate measures**: How do variables relate to each other?

Our goal is not only to calculate statistics, but to use visualization to reveal the stories contained in the data!

## Time Series Features

A time series is a sequence of data points recorded or measured in chronological order, usually at regular, equally spaced intervals.

- Trend: A trend exists when there is a long-term increase or decrease in the data. 

- Seasonality: Regular patterns that repeat over fixed periods like days, months, or years.

- Cyclic: Long-term ups and downs that do not follow a fixed seasonal schedule.

- Irregular: Random, unpredictable short-term changes

## Time plot

::: {.notes}

For time series data, the obvious graph to start with is a time plot. That is, the observations are plotted against the time of observation, with consecutive observations joined by straight lines.

:::


## Time Series - Seasonality 

```{r}
# ================================================================
# SEASONAL PLOT: AIRPASSENGERS
# Complete visualization for a Data Visualization class
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ================================================================
# 1. LOAD THE BUILT-IN AIRPASSENGERS DATA
# ================================================================

data("AirPassengers")

# ================================================================
# 2. CONVERT THE TIME SERIES INTO A DATA FRAME
#
# Each observation is described by:
# - calendar year;
# - seasonal position, represented by month;
# - number of passengers.
# ================================================================

air_seasonal_data <- tibble(
  Year = floor(
    as.numeric(
      time(AirPassengers)
    )
  ),

  Month_number = as.integer(
    cycle(AirPassengers)
  ),

  Passengers = as.numeric(
    AirPassengers
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    Month = factor(
      Month_number,

      levels = 1:12,

      labels = month.abb,

      ordered = TRUE
    ),

    Year_factor = factor(
      Year
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 3. VALIDATE THE DATA STRUCTURE
# ================================================================

stopifnot(
  nrow(air_seasonal_data) ==
    length(AirPassengers),

  n_distinct(
    air_seasonal_data$Month
  ) == 12,

  all(
    air_seasonal_data |>
      count(Year) |>
      pull(n) == 12
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 4. CALCULATE TEACHING SUMMARY VALUES
# ================================================================

first_year <- min(
  air_seasonal_data$Year
)

last_year <- max(
  air_seasonal_data$Year
)

minimum_passengers <- min(
  air_seasonal_data$Passengers
)

maximum_passengers <- max(
  air_seasonal_data$Passengers
)

maximum_observation <- air_seasonal_data |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = Passengers,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  )

minimum_observation <- air_seasonal_data |>
  slice_min(
    order_by = Passengers,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  )

# ================================================================
# 5. CREATE DATA FOR THE FIRST AND LAST YEARS
#
# These lines are redrawn with greater emphasis to make the
# evolution of the seasonal pattern easier to recognize.
# ================================================================

first_year_data <- air_seasonal_data |>
  filter(
    Year == first_year
  )

last_year_data <- air_seasonal_data |>
  filter(
    Year == last_year
  )

# ================================================================
# 6. CREATE LABEL POSITIONS
# ================================================================

maximum_label <- maximum_observation |>
  mutate(
    Label = paste0(
      "Maximum: ",
      comma(Passengers),
      "\n",
      as.character(Month),
      " ",
      Year
    )
  )

minimum_label <- minimum_observation |>
  mutate(
    Label = paste0(
      "Minimum: ",
      comma(Passengers),
      "\n",
      as.character(Month),
      " ",
      Year
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 7. BUILD THE SEASONAL PLOT
# ================================================================

air_seasonal_plot <- ggplot(
  data = air_seasonal_data,

  aes(
    x = Month,
    y = Passengers,
    group = Year,
    color = Year
  )
) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Connect monthly observations within each year
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.85,
    alpha = 0.72,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Preserve the individual monthly observations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    size = 1.9,
    alpha = 0.78
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Emphasize the first year
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    data = first_year_data,

    aes(
      x = Month,
      y = Passengers,
      group = Year
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#64748B",
    linewidth = 1.15,
    linetype = "dashed",
    lineend = "round"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = first_year_data,

    aes(
      x = Month,
      y = Passengers
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#64748B",
    fill = "white",
    shape = 21,
    size = 2.4,
    stroke = 0.8
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Emphasize the most recent year
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    data = last_year_data,

    aes(
      x = Month,
      y = Passengers,
      group = Year
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#B2182B",
    linewidth = 1.35,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = last_year_data,

    aes(
      x = Month,
      y = Passengers
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#B2182B",
    fill = "white",
    shape = 21,
    size = 2.7,
    stroke = 0.9
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Highlight the maximum observed value
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = maximum_observation,

    aes(
      x = Month,
      y = Passengers
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#B2182B",
    fill = "#FEE2E2",
    shape = 21,
    size = 4,
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +

  geom_label(
    data = maximum_label,

    aes(
      x = Month,
      y = Passengers,
      label = Label
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#991B1B",
    fill = "white",
    label.size = 0.25,
    label.padding = grid::unit(
      0.18,
      "lines"
    ),
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    nudge_x = -0.55,
    nudge_y = 28
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Highlight the minimum observed value
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = minimum_observation,

    aes(
      x = Month,
      y = Passengers
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#1D4ED8",
    fill = "#DBEAFE",
    shape = 21,
    size = 4,
    stroke = 1.1
  ) +

  geom_label(
    data = minimum_label,

    aes(
      x = Month,
      y = Passengers,
      label = Label
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#1D4ED8",
    fill = "white",
    label.size = 0.25,
    label.padding = grid::unit(
      0.18,
      "lines"
    ),
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold",
    nudge_x = 0.75,
    nudge_y = 24
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Continuous color scale represents chronological progression
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_color_gradientn(
    colors = c(
      "#CBD5E1",
      "#93C5FD",
      "#2F6FA5",
      "#173F73",
      "#B2182B"
    ),

    breaks = pretty(
      unique(
        air_seasonal_data$Year
      ),
      n = 6
    ),

    limits = c(
      first_year,
      last_year
    ),

    name = "Year"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Vertical scale
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(
      accuracy = 1,
      big.mark = ","
    ),

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.04,
        0.14
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Titles and labels
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  labs(
    title =
      "How Does Air Travel Vary Within Each Year?",

    subtitle = paste0(
      "Seasonal plot of monthly international airline passengers, ",
      first_year,
      "–",
      last_year
    ),

    x = "Month",

    y = "Passengers (thousands)",

    caption = paste0(
      "Each line represents one year. ",
      "The dashed gray line is ",
      first_year,
      "; the solid red line is ",
      last_year,
      "."
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Presentation theme
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 13
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#172033",
      margin = margin(
        b = 4
      )
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11.5,
      color = "#475569",
      margin = margin(
        b = 14
      )
    ),

    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 8.5,
      color = "#64748B",
      hjust = 0,
      lineheight = 1.15,
      margin = margin(
        t = 10
      )
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#334155"
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 9,
      color = "#64748B"
    ),

    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(
      color = "#E5E7EB",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),

    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      color = "#E5E7EB",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    legend.position = "right",

    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 10,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#334155"
    ),

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 8.5,
      color = "#64748B"
    ),

    legend.key.height = grid::unit(
      1.2,
      "cm"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 18,
      b = 8,
      l = 10
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 8. DISPLAY THE FIGURE
# ================================================================

air_seasonal_plot
```

## Time Series - Seasonality 

```{r}
#| label: air-passengers-seasonal-subseries


# ================================================================
# SEASONAL SUBSERIES PLOT: AIRPASSENGERS
# Complete figure for a Data Visualization class
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ================================================================
# 1. LOAD THE BUILT-IN AIRPASSENGERS DATA
# ================================================================

data("AirPassengers")

# ================================================================
# 2. CONVERT THE TIME SERIES INTO A DATA FRAME
#
# AirPassengers is a monthly time series containing international
# airline passenger totals, measured in thousands.
# ================================================================

air_subseries_data <- tibble(
  Date = seq.Date(
    from = as.Date("1949-01-01"),
    by = "month",
    length.out = length(AirPassengers)
  ),

  Year = floor(
    as.numeric(
      time(AirPassengers)
    )
  ),

  Month_number = as.integer(
    cycle(AirPassengers)
  ),

  Passengers = as.numeric(
    AirPassengers
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    Month = factor(
      Month_number,
      levels = 1:12,
      labels = month.abb,
      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 3. VALIDATE THE TIME-SERIES STRUCTURE
# ================================================================

stopifnot(
  nrow(air_subseries_data) ==
    length(AirPassengers),

  n_distinct(
    air_subseries_data$Month
  ) == 12,

  all(
    air_subseries_data |>
      count(Year) |>
      pull(n) == 12
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 4. CALCULATE THE MEAN FOR EACH SEASONAL POSITION
#
# For monthly data, each seasonal position corresponds to a month.
# The horizontal reference line in each panel represents the mean
# passenger volume for that month across all years.
# ================================================================

monthly_means <- air_subseries_data |>
  group_by(Month) |>
  summarise(
    Monthly_mean = mean(
      Passengers,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Minimum = min(
      Passengers,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Maximum = max(
      Passengers,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Observations = n(),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

# ================================================================
# 5. JOIN THE MONTHLY MEANS TO THE OBSERVATIONS
# ================================================================

air_subseries_data <- air_subseries_data |>
  left_join(
    monthly_means |>
      select(
        Month,
        Monthly_mean
      ),
    by = "Month"
  )

# ================================================================
# 6. IDENTIFY THE FIRST AND LAST OBSERVATIONS IN EACH MONTH
#
# These points help demonstrate how each monthly subseries evolves
# from the beginning to the end of the sample.
# ================================================================

first_monthly_observations <- air_subseries_data |>
  group_by(Month) |>
  slice_min(
    order_by = Year,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  ungroup()

last_monthly_observations <- air_subseries_data |>
  group_by(Month) |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = Year,
    n = 1,
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# ================================================================
# 7. CREATE LABELS FOR THE MONTHLY MEANS
# ================================================================

monthly_mean_labels <- monthly_means |>
  mutate(
    Mean_label = paste0(
      "Mean: ",
      comma(
        Monthly_mean,
        accuracy = 1
      )
    ),

    Label_year = max(
      air_subseries_data$Year
    ) + 0.35
  )

# ================================================================
# 8. CREATE THE SEASONAL SUBSERIES PLOT
# ================================================================

air_subseries_plot <- ggplot(
  data = air_subseries_data,
  aes(
    x = Year,
    y = Passengers
  )
) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Monthly mean reference
  #
  # Each panel receives a different horizontal mean.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_hline(
    data = monthly_means,
    aes(
      yintercept = Monthly_mean
    ),
    color = "#2F6FA5",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Time evolution within each seasonal position
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    color = "#64748B",
    linewidth = 0.75,
    alpha = 0.80,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Preserve the individual annual observations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    color = "#64748B",
    fill = "white",
    shape = 21,
    size = 2.1,
    stroke = 0.65,
    alpha = 0.90
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Highlight the first observation in each month
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = first_monthly_observations,
    aes(
      x = Year,
      y = Passengers
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#64748B",
    fill = "#F8FAFC",
    shape = 21,
    size = 2.7,
    stroke = 0.9
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Highlight the final observation in each month
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = last_monthly_observations,
    aes(
      x = Year,
      y = Passengers
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#B2182B",
    fill = "#FEE2E2",
    shape = 21,
    size = 2.9,
    stroke = 1
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Label the monthly mean inside each panel
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_text(
    data = monthly_mean_labels,
    aes(
      x = Label_year,
      y = Monthly_mean,
      label = Mean_label
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#1D4ED8",
    size = 2.7,
    fontface = "bold",
    hjust = 0,
    vjust = -0.35
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Create one mini time plot for each month
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  facet_wrap(
    facets = vars(Month),
    ncol = 4,
    scales = "free_y",
    labeller = label_value
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Configure the year axis
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = c(
      1950,
      1955,
      1960
    ),

    limits = c(
      min(
        air_subseries_data$Year
      ),
      max(
        air_subseries_data$Year
      ) + 1.25
    ),

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.02,
        0.01
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Configure the passenger axis
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(
      accuracy = 1,
      big.mark = ","
    ),

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.12,
        0.18
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Titles and labels
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  labs(
    title =
      "How Does Each Month Change Over Time?",

    subtitle = paste0(
      "Seasonal subseries plot of AirPassengers | ",
      "Horizontal blue lines show the mean for each month"
    ),

    x = "Year",

    y = "Passengers (thousands)",

    caption = paste0(
      "Each panel contains observations from the same month across ",
      "different years. Gray lines show temporal evolution; ",
      "blue lines show monthly means; red points identify 1960."
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Presentation theme
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 12
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#172033",
      margin = margin(
        b = 4
      )
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11.5,
      color = "#475569",
      margin = margin(
        b = 14
      )
    ),

    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 8.5,
      color = "#64748B",
      hjust = 0,
      lineheight = 1.15,
      margin = margin(
        t = 10
      )
    ),

    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#F3F8FC",
      color = "#CBD5E1",
      linewidth = 0.55
    ),

    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 10.5,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#173F73",
      margin = margin(
        t = 5,
        r = 5,
        b = 5,
        l = 5
      )
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 10.5,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#334155"
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 8,
      color = "#64748B"
    ),

    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(
      color = "#E5E7EB",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),

    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      color = "#E5E7EB",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),

    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

    panel.spacing = grid::unit(
      0.8,
      "lines"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 20,
      b = 8,
      l = 10
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 9. DISPLAY THE FIGURE
# ================================================================

air_subseries_plot
```


## Box-Cox Transformation

**Box-Cox transformations** includes logarithmic and power
transformations controlled by $\lambda$

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="57%"}

### Definition

$$
\boxed{
w_t =
\begin{cases}
\log(y_t),
& \lambda = 0, \\[4pt]
\dfrac{
\operatorname{sign}(y_t)\lvert y_t\rvert^\lambda - 1
}{
\lambda
},
& \lambda \neq 0.
\end{cases}
}
$$

This modified formulation allows negative values of $y_t$, provided that

$$
\lambda > 0.
$$


:::

::: {.column width="43%"}

### Role of $\lambda$

$$
\begin{array}{ccl}
\lambda = 1
&\Rightarrow&
w_t = y_t - 1
\\[3pt]
\lambda = 0
&\Rightarrow&
w_t = \log(y_t)
\\[3pt]
\lambda \neq 0
&\Rightarrow&
\text{power transformation}
\end{array}
$$

- $\lambda = 1$ changes only the **level**

- $\lambda = 0$ applies a **log transformation**

- $\lambda \neq 0$ change the **shape and scale**

:::

::::

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" icon="false"}
Choose $\lambda$ to **stabilize the variance**, reduce scale-dependent
fluctuations, and make the variation more consistent over time.
:::

<small>
Box & Cox (1964); modified transformation from Bickel & Doksum (1981).
</small>

## Box-Cox Transformation

```{r}
# ============================================================
# BOX-COX TRANSFORMATION
# Illustration of variance stabilization over time
# ============================================================

# 1. Packages -------------------------------------------------

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(slider)
library(forecast)
library(patchwork)
library(scales)

# 2. Reproducibility ------------------------------------------

set.seed(42)

# 3. Generate an illustrative positive time series ------------

n <- 180

data_boxcox <- tibble(
  Time = 1:n,

  # Exponentially increasing level
  Level = 18 * exp(0.012 * Time),

  # Multiplicative seasonal component
  Seasonality = 1 + 0.16 * sin(2 * pi * Time / 12),

  # Multiplicative random variation
  Noise = exp(rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 0.16)),

  # Observed positive series
  Original = Level * Seasonality * Noise
)

# 4. Estimate the Box-Cox lambda -------------------------------

lambda <- forecast::BoxCox.lambda(
  x      = ts(data_boxcox$Original, frequency = 12),
  method = "guerrero",
  lower  = -2,
  upper  = 2
)

# 5. Apply the Box-Cox transformation --------------------------

data_boxcox <- data_boxcox |>
  mutate(
    BoxCox = forecast::BoxCox(
      Original,
      lambda = lambda
    )
  )

# 6. Calculate rolling standard deviations --------------------

rolling_window <- 18

data_boxcox <- data_boxcox |>
  mutate(
    SD_Original = slide_dbl(
      Original,
      sd,
      .before   = floor(rolling_window / 2),
      .after    = floor(rolling_window / 2) - 1,
      .complete = TRUE
    ),

    SD_BoxCox = slide_dbl(
      BoxCox,
      sd,
      .before   = floor(rolling_window / 2),
      .after    = floor(rolling_window / 2) - 1,
      .complete = TRUE
    ),

    Original_Lower = Original - SD_Original,
    Original_Upper = Original + SD_Original,

    BoxCox_Lower = BoxCox - SD_BoxCox,
    BoxCox_Upper = BoxCox + SD_BoxCox
  )

# 7. Compare early and late variability ------------------------

comparison_window <- 45

sd_early_original <- data_boxcox |>
  slice_head(n = comparison_window) |>
  summarise(value = sd(Original)) |>
  pull(value)

sd_late_original <- data_boxcox |>
  slice_tail(n = comparison_window) |>
  summarise(value = sd(Original)) |>
  pull(value)

sd_early_boxcox <- data_boxcox |>
  slice_head(n = comparison_window) |>
  summarise(value = sd(BoxCox)) |>
  pull(value)

sd_late_boxcox <- data_boxcox |>
  slice_tail(n = comparison_window) |>
  summarise(value = sd(BoxCox)) |>
  pull(value)

ratio_original <- sd_late_original / sd_early_original
ratio_boxcox   <- sd_late_boxcox / sd_early_boxcox

# 8. Color palette ---------------------------------------------

color_navy  <- "#17324D"
color_teal  <- "#00A6A6"
color_coral <- "#EF6C5B"
color_grey  <- "#6B7280"
color_panel <- "#F4F7FA"

# 9. Common theme ----------------------------------------------

theme_boxcox <- theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(

# 10. Original-scale plot --------------------------------------

plot_original <- ggplot(
  data_boxcox,
  aes(x = Time, y = Original)
) +
  annotate(
    "rect",
    xmin  = 1,
```

## Index

```{r}
# ================================================================
# DAILY TO MONTHLY DATA
# Monthly prices and compounded monthly returns
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

# ================================================================
# 1. IDENTIFY THE PRICE COLUMN
#
# The code searches for common price-column names.
# Place the exact name used in your dataset first if necessary.
# ================================================================

price_candidates <- c(
  "adjusted_prices",
  "adjusted_price",
  "price_adjusted",
  "adj_price",
  "adjusted_close",
  "price",
  "Price",
  "close",
  "Close"
)

price_column <- intersect(
  price_candidates,
  names(dados)
)

if (length(price_column) == 0L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "No price column was found. Available columns are: ",
      paste(
        names(dados),
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}

price_column <- price_column[1]

# ================================================================
# 2. VALIDATE THE REQUIRED COLUMNS
# ================================================================

required_columns <- c(
  "ticker",
  "ref_date",
  "ret_adjusted_prices"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(dados)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The following required columns are missing: ",
      paste(
        missing_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 3. HELPER FUNCTION
#
# Returns the last finite observation in a vector.
# ================================================================

last_finite <- function(x) {

  x <- as.numeric(x)

  valid_positions <- which(
    is.finite(x)
  )

  if (length(valid_positions) == 0L) {
    return(NA_real_)
  }

  x[
    valid_positions[
      length(valid_positions)
    ]
  ]
}

# ================================================================
# 4. PREPARE THE DAILY DATA
#
# The price column is renamed to adjusted_price.
# The return column is renamed to adjusted_return.
# ================================================================

daily_data <- dados |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker),
    ref_date = as.Date(ref_date),
    adjusted_price = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(
        .data[[price_column]]
      )
    ),

    adjusted_return = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(
        ret_adjusted_prices
      )
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ticker),
    ticker != "",
    !is.na(ref_date)
  ) |>
  arrange(
    ticker,
    ref_date
  )

if (nrow(daily_data) == 0L) {
  stop(
    "No valid ticker and date observations were found."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 5. AGGREGATE DUPLICATE TICKER-DATE OBSERVATIONS
#
# If duplicate observations exist on the same date, the mean of
# the finite values is used.
# ================================================================

daily_data <- daily_data |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    ref_date
  ) |>
  summarise(
    adjusted_price = {
      valid_values <- adjusted_price[
        is.finite(adjusted_price)
      ]
      if (length(valid_values) == 0L) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        mean(valid_values)
      }
    },
    adjusted_return = {
      valid_values <- adjusted_return[
        is.finite(adjusted_return)
      ]
      if (length(valid_values) == 0L) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        mean(valid_values)
      }
    },

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    month = floor_date(
      ref_date,
      unit = "month"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(
    ticker,
    ref_date
  )

# ================================================================
# 6. CREATE MONTHLY PRICES
#
# The monthly price is the last valid price observed in the month.
# The actual observation date is preserved.
# ================================================================

monthly_prices <- daily_data |>
  filter(
    is.finite(adjusted_price)
  ) |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    month
  ) |>
  arrange(
    ref_date,
    .by_group = TRUE
  ) |>
  summarise(
    monthly_price_date = ref_date[
      length(ref_date)
    ],

    monthly_adjusted_price = last_finite(
      adjusted_price
    ),

    first_adjusted_price = adjusted_price[1],

    average_adjusted_price = mean(
      adjusted_price
    ),

    minimum_adjusted_price = min(
      adjusted_price
    ),

    maximum_adjusted_price = max(
      adjusted_price
    ),

    price_observations = n(),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(
    ticker,
    month
  )

if (nrow(monthly_prices) == 0L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "No finite prices were found in column '",
      price_column,
      "'."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 7. CALCULATE MONTHLY RETURNS FROM MONTH-END PRICES
#
# R_m = P_m / P_(m-1) - 1
# ================================================================

monthly_prices <- monthly_prices |>
  group_by(ticker) |>
  arrange(
    month,
    .by_group = TRUE
  ) |>
  mutate(
    previous_monthly_price = lag(
      monthly_adjusted_price
    ),

    monthly_return_from_price = if_else(
      is.finite(previous_monthly_price) &
        previous_monthly_price != 0,

      monthly_adjusted_price /
        previous_monthly_price -
        1,

      NA_real_
    ),

    monthly_log_return_from_price = if_else(
      is.finite(previous_monthly_price) &
        previous_monthly_price > 0 &
        monthly_adjusted_price > 0,

      log(
        monthly_adjusted_price /
          previous_monthly_price
      ),

      NA_real_
    )
  ) |>
  ungroup()

# ================================================================
# 8. COMPOUND DAILY SIMPLE RETURNS WITHIN EACH MONTH
#
# R_m = product(1 + r_d) - 1
#
# This calculation assumes that ret_adjusted_prices contains
# decimal simple returns:
#
#  0.01  =  1%
# -0.02  = -2%
# ================================================================

monthly_returns <- daily_data |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    month
  ) |>
  summarise(
    valid_daily_returns = sum(
      is.finite(adjusted_return)
    ),

    first_return_date = {
      valid_dates <- ref_date[
        is.finite(adjusted_return)
      ]

      if (length(valid_dates) == 0L) {
        as.Date(NA)
      } else {
        min(valid_dates)
      }
    },

    last_return_date = {
      valid_dates <- ref_date[
        is.finite(adjusted_return)
      ]

      if (length(valid_dates) == 0L) {
        as.Date(NA)
      } else {
        max(valid_dates)
      }
    },

    monthly_adjusted_return = {
      valid_returns <- adjusted_return[
        is.finite(adjusted_return)
      ]

      if (length(valid_returns) == 0L) {
        NA_real_
      } else if (any(valid_returns <= -1)) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        prod(
          1 + valid_returns
        ) - 1
      }
    },

    monthly_log_return = {
      valid_returns <- adjusted_return[
        is.finite(adjusted_return) &
          adjusted_return > -1
      ]

      if (length(valid_returns) == 0L) {
        NA_real_
      } else {
        sum(
          log1p(valid_returns)
        )
      }
    },

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(
    ticker,
    month
  ) |>
  mutate(
    monthly_simple_return_from_logs = if_else(
      is.finite(monthly_log_return),

      expm1(
        monthly_log_return
      ),

      NA_real_
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 9. COMBINE MONTHLY PRICES AND RETURNS
# ================================================================

monthly_data <- monthly_prices |>
  full_join(
    monthly_returns,
    by = c(
      "ticker",
      "month"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(
    ticker,
    month
  )

# ================================================================
# 10. COMPARE THE TWO MONTHLY-RETURN CALCULATIONS
#
# The two returns should be close when:
#
# - daily returns were calculated from the same adjusted prices;
# - the first daily return captures the movement from the final
#   price of the previous month;
# - no relevant daily observations are missing;
# - both series use the same adjustment methodology.
# ================================================================

monthly_data <- monthly_data |>
  mutate(
    return_difference =
      monthly_adjusted_return -
      monthly_return_from_price,

    absolute_return_difference = abs(
      return_difference
    ),

    return_calculations_match = case_when(
      is.na(monthly_adjusted_return) |
        is.na(monthly_return_from_price) ~
        NA,

      absolute_return_difference <
        1e-8 ~
        TRUE,

      TRUE ~
        FALSE
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 11. VALIDATE THE MONTHLY DATASET
# ================================================================

duplicated_months <- monthly_data |>
  count(
    ticker,
    month
  ) |>
  filter(
    n > 1L
  )

if (nrow(duplicated_months) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "The monthly dataset contains duplicated ticker-month pairs."
  )
}

stopifnot(
  all(
    monthly_data$monthly_adjusted_price[
      !is.na(
        monthly_data$monthly_adjusted_price
      )
    ] > 0
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 12. FINAL MONTHLY DATASET
# ================================================================

monthly_data <- monthly_data |>
  select(
    ticker,
    month,

    monthly_price_date,
    monthly_adjusted_price,

    first_adjusted_price,
    average_adjusted_price,
    minimum_adjusted_price,
    maximum_adjusted_price,
    price_observations,

    previous_monthly_price,
    monthly_return_from_price,
    monthly_log_return_from_price,

    first_return_date,
    last_return_date,
    valid_daily_returns,
    monthly_adjusted_return,
    monthly_log_return,
    monthly_simple_return_from_logs,

    return_difference,
    absolute_return_difference,
    return_calculations_match
  )

# ================================================================
# 13. DISPLAY THE COMPLETE RESULT
# ================================================================

monthly_data
```



## Technical Indicators

The simple moving average assigns equal weight to the $w$ most recent observations:

$$
\operatorname{MA}_{t}^{(w)}
=
\frac{1}{w}
\sum_{j=0}^{w-1}Y_{t-j}.
$$

<!-- Each observation remains in the calculation for exactly $w$ periods and receives weight $1/w$ -->

The exponential moving average assigns greater weight to more recent observations:

$$
\operatorname{EMA}_{t}
=
\alpha Y_t
+
(1-\alpha)\operatorname{EMA}_{t-1},
\qquad
0<\alpha\leq1.
$$

<!-- A larger $\alpha$ responds more quickly to recent changes, while a smaller $\alpha$ produces a smoother estimate -->

> **The same weighting principles can be applied to other local measures. Moving means track changes in local position, while moving standard deviations track changes in local dispersion.**


## Technical Indicators

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ================================================================
# 1. PARAMETERS
# ================================================================

window_size <- 21L

# Conventional equivalence between an EMA span and alpha
alpha <- 2 / (window_size + 1)

# ================================================================
# 2. IDENTIFY THE PRICE COLUMN
#
# The first matching column is selected.
# Add the actual name to this vector if necessary.
# ================================================================

price_candidates <- c(
  "adjusted_prices",
  "adjusted_price",
  "price_adjusted",
  "adj_price",
  "adjusted_close",
  "price",
  "Price",
  "close",
  "Close"
)

price_column <- price_candidates[
  price_candidates %in% names(dados)
][1]

if (
  length(price_column) == 0 ||
  is.na(price_column)
) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "No price column was found. Available columns are: ",
      paste(
        names(dados),
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 3. SELECT THE FIRST VALID TICKER
# ================================================================

ticker_selected <- dados |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ticker)
  ) |>
  distinct(ticker) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  pull(ticker) |>
  as.character()

if (
  length(ticker_selected) == 0 ||
  is.na(ticker_selected)
) {
  stop(
    "No valid ticker was found in the dataset."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 4. PREPARE THE PRICE SERIES
#
# If duplicate prices exist for the same date and ticker,
# their mean is used to create one price per date.
# ================================================================

technical_data <- dados |>
  filter(
    ticker == ticker_selected,
    !is.na(ref_date),
    !is.na(.data[[price_column]]),
    is.finite(
      as.numeric(
        .data[[price_column]]
      )
    )
  ) |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker),
    ref_date = as.Date(ref_date),
    price = as.numeric(
      .data[[price_column]]
    )
  ) |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    ref_date
  ) |>
  summarise(
    price = mean(
      price,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(ref_date) %>% 
  filter(ref_date > as.Date("2025-01-01"))

n_observations <- nrow(
  technical_data
)

if (n_observations < window_size) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least ",
      window_size,
      " valid price observations are required for ",
      ticker_selected,
      ". Only ",
      n_observations,
      " were found."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 5. TRAILING SIMPLE MOVING AVERAGE
#
# MA_t = mean of the latest w observations, including time t.
# ================================================================

trailing_mean <- function(x, window) {

  n <- length(x)

  result <- rep(
    NA_real_,
    n
  )

  if (n >= window) {

    for (i in seq.int(window, n)) {

      result[i] <- mean(
        x[(i - window + 1):i],
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    }
  }

  result
}

# ================================================================
# 6. TRAILING ROLLING STANDARD DEVIATION
#
# The sample standard deviation is calculated over the same
# trailing window used by the simple moving average.
# ================================================================

trailing_sd <- function(x, window) {

  n <- length(x)

  result <- rep(
    NA_real_,
    n
  )

  if (n >= window) {

    for (i in seq.int(window, n)) {

      result[i] <- sd(
        x[(i - window + 1):i],
        na.rm = TRUE
      )
    }
  }

  result
}

# ================================================================
# 7. EXPONENTIAL MOVING AVERAGE
#
# EMA_t = alpha * P_t + (1 - alpha) * EMA_(t-1)
# ================================================================

exponential_mean <- function(x, alpha) {

  n <- length(x)

  result <- rep(
    NA_real_,
    n
  )

  result[1] <- x[1]

  if (n >= 2) {

    for (i in 2:n) {

      result[i] <-
        alpha * x[i] +
        (1 - alpha) * result[i - 1]
    }
  }

  result
}

# ================================================================
# 8. EXPONENTIALLY WEIGHTED STANDARD DEVIATION
#
# The recursive exponential variance is:
#
# V_t = (1 - alpha) *
#       [V_(t-1) + alpha * (P_t - EMA_(t-1))^2]
#
# EWSD_t = sqrt(V_t)
# ================================================================

exponential_sd <- function(x, alpha) {

  n <- length(x)

  exponential_average <- rep(
    NA_real_,
    n
  )

  exponential_variance <- rep(
    NA_real_,
    n
  )

  exponential_average[1] <- x[1]

  exponential_variance[1] <- 0

  if (n >= 2) {

    for (i in 2:n) {

      previous_mean <-
        exponential_average[i - 1]

      previous_variance <-
        exponential_variance[i - 1]

      exponential_average[i] <-
        alpha * x[i] +
        (1 - alpha) * previous_mean

      exponential_variance[i] <-
        (1 - alpha) * (
          previous_variance +
            alpha *
              (x[i] - previous_mean)^2
        )
    }
  }

  sqrt(
    pmax(
      exponential_variance,
      0
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 9. CALCULATE ALL PRICE INDICATORS
# ================================================================

technical_data <- technical_data |>
  mutate(
    MA = trailing_mean(
      price,
      window = window_size
    ),

    EMA = exponential_mean(
      price,
      alpha = alpha
    ),

    Rolling_SD = trailing_sd(
      price,
      window = window_size
    ),

    Exponential_SD = exponential_sd(
      price,
      alpha = alpha
    ),

    MA_lower = MA - Rolling_SD,

    MA_upper = MA + Rolling_SD,

    EMA_lower = EMA - Exponential_SD,

    EMA_upper = EMA + Exponential_SD
  )

# ================================================================
# 10. VALIDATE THE INDICATORS
# ================================================================

expected_complete_windows <-
  n_observations -
  window_size +
  1L

stopifnot(
  nrow(technical_data) ==
    n_observations,

  sum(
    !is.na(
      technical_data$MA
    )
  ) ==
    expected_complete_windows,

  sum(
    !is.na(
      technical_data$Rolling_SD
    )
  ) ==
    expected_complete_windows,

  all(
    technical_data$Rolling_SD[
      !is.na(
        technical_data$Rolling_SD
      )
    ] >= 0
  ),

  all(
    technical_data$Exponential_SD[
      !is.na(
        technical_data$Exponential_SD
      )
    ] >= 0
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 11. DETERMINE A SUITABLE PRICE FORMAT
#
# Large price values are displayed with no decimals.
# Smaller values retain greater precision.
# ================================================================

median_price <- median(
  technical_data$price,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

price_accuracy <- case_when(
  median_price >= 100 ~ 1,
  median_price >= 10 ~ 0.1,
  TRUE ~ 0.01
)

price_label_function <- label_number(
  accuracy = price_accuracy,
  big.mark = ","
)

# ================================================================
# 12. CREATE THE SINGLE FIGURE
# ================================================================

technical_indicators_plot <- ggplot(
  data = technical_data,
  aes(x = ref_date)
) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # SIMPLE MOVING-AVERAGE DISPERSION BAND
  #
  # MA_t plus or minus rolling SD_t
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = MA_lower,
      ymax = MA_upper,
      fill = "MA ± rolling SD"
    ),
    alpha = 0.17,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # EXPONENTIALLY WEIGHTED DISPERSION BAND
  #
  # EMA_t plus or minus exponentially weighted SD_t
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = EMA_lower,
      ymax = EMA_upper,
      fill = "EMA ± exponentially weighted SD"
    ),
    alpha = 0.13,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # OBSERVED PRICE
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = price,
      color = "Observed price",
      linewidth = "Observed price"
    ),
    alpha = 0.58,
    lineend = "round",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # SIMPLE MOVING AVERAGE
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = MA,
      color = "Simple moving average",
      linewidth = "Simple moving average"
    ),
    lineend = "round",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # EXPONENTIAL MOVING AVERAGE
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = EMA,
      color = "Exponential moving average",
      linewidth = "Exponential moving average"
    ),
    lineend = "round",
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # LINE COLORS
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,

    values = c(
      "Observed price" = "#64748B",
      "Simple moving average" = "#2F6FA5",
      "Exponential moving average" = "#D97706"
    ),

    breaks = c(
      "Observed price",
      "Simple moving average",
      "Exponential moving average"
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # BAND COLORS
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_fill_manual(
    name = NULL,

    values = c(
      "MA ± rolling SD" = "#2F6FA5",
      "EMA ± exponentially weighted SD" = "#D97706"
    ),

    breaks = c(
      "MA ± rolling SD",
      "EMA ± exponentially weighted SD"
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # LINE WIDTHS
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_linewidth_manual(
    name = NULL,

    values = c(
      "Observed price" = 0.55,
      "Simple moving average" = 1.10,
      "Exponential moving average" = 1.10
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # DATE AXIS
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "6 months",

    date_minor_breaks = "3 months",

    date_labels = "%b\n%Y",

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.01,
        0.02
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # PRICE AXIS
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = price_label_function,

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.06,
        0.10
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # TITLES
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  labs(
    title =
      "How Do Moving Indicators Track Local Price and Dispersion?",

    subtitle = paste0(
      ticker_selected,
      " price | ",
      window_size,
      "-observation trailing window | ",
      "EMA alpha = ",
      number(
        alpha,
        accuracy = 0.001
      )
    ),

    x = "Date",

    y = "Price",

    caption = paste0(
      "Solid lines represent observed and smoothed prices. ",
      "Shaded areas represent one local standard deviation ",
      "above and below each moving average."
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # PRESENTATION THEME
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 13
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#172033",
      margin = margin(
        b = 4
      )
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11.5,

      margin = margin(
        b = 13
      )
    ),

    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 8.5,
      color = "#64748B",
      hjust = 0,
      lineheight = 1.15,
      margin = margin(
        t = 10
      )
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#334155"
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 8.5,
      color = "#64748B"
    ),

    panel.grid.major = element_line(
      color = "#E5E7EB",

    ),

    panel.grid.minor.x = element_line(

# ================================================================

technical_indicators_plot
```

## Time Series Decomposition

A time series $Y_t$ might be decomposed into three additive components

$$
Y_t = T_t +S_t + R_t
$$
where $T_t$, $S_t$, and $R_t$ are the trend, seasonal and the remainder, respectively.

Let $m$ denote the seasonal period. The components can be estimated as follows:

1. Trend: $\hat{T}_t = \frac{1}{m} \sum_{j=-\lfloor m/2 \rfloor}^{\lfloor m/2 \rfloor} Y_{t+j}$, where a centered moving average smooths short-term and seasonal fluctuations.

2. Detrended series: $D_t = Y_t-\widehat{T}_t.$ For each seasonal position $k=1,\ldots,m$.

3. Seasonal component:$\widetilde{S}_k = \frac{1}{n_k} \sum_{t:\,s(t)=k} D_t$, and centering the resulting seasonal indices: $\widehat{S}_k = \widetilde{S}_k - \frac{1}{m} \sum_{\ell=1}^{m}\widetilde{S}_{\ell}, \qquad \sum_{k=1}^{m}\widehat{S}_k=0.$

4. Remainder: $\widehat{R}_t = Y_t-\widehat{T}_t-\widehat{S}_{s(t)}$  

## Time Series Decomposition

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(scales)

# Load the built-in monthly time series
data("AirPassengers")

# Convert the time-series index to monthly dates
air_data <- tibble(
  Date = seq.Date(
    from = as.Date("1949-01-01"),
    by = "month",
    length.out = length(AirPassengers)
  ),
  Passengers = as.numeric(AirPassengers),
  Log_Passengers = log(as.numeric(AirPassengers))
)

# STL decomposition on the log scale
# The log transformation stabilizes the increasing seasonal amplitude
air_stl <- stl(
  ts(
    air_data$Log_Passengers,
    start = c(1949, 1),
    frequency = 12
  ),
  s.window = "periodic",
  robust = TRUE
)

# Extract the STL components
air_components <- air_data |>
  mutate(
    Observed = Log_Passengers,
    Trend = as.numeric(
      air_stl$time.series[, "trend"]
    ),
    Seasonal = as.numeric(
      air_stl$time.series[, "seasonal"]
    ),
    Remainder = as.numeric(
      air_stl$time.series[, "remainder"]
    ),
    Reconstructed = Trend + Seasonal + Remainder
  )

# Validate the additive identity
reconstruction_error <- max(
  abs(
    air_components$Observed -
      air_components$Reconstructed
  ),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

stopifnot(
  reconstruction_error < 1e-10
)

# Convert the components to long format
air_components_long <- air_components |>
  select(
    Date,
    Observed,
    Trend,
    Seasonal,
    Remainder
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(
      Observed,
      Trend,
      Seasonal,
      Remainder
    ),
    names_to = "Component_code",
    values_to = "Value"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Component = factor(
      Component_code,
      levels = c(
        "Observed",
        "Trend",
        "Seasonal",
        "Remainder"
      ),
      labels = c(
        "Observed series: Yt",
        "Trend component: Tt",
        "Seasonal component: St",
        "Remainder component: Rt"
      )
    ),
    Component_code = factor(
      Component_code,
      levels = c(
        "Observed",
        "Trend",
        "Seasonal",
        "Remainder"
      )
    )
  )

# Zero-reference lines for seasonal and remainder panels
zero_lines <- tibble(
  Component = factor(
    c(
      "Seasonal component: St",
      "Remainder component: Rt"
    ),
    levels = levels(
      air_components_long$Component
    )
  ),
  Reference = 0
)

# Robustly identify unusual remainder observations
remainder_center <- median(
  air_components$Remainder,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

remainder_scale <- mad(
  air_components$Remainder,
  center = remainder_center,
  constant = 1.4826,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Fallback if MAD is zero or invalid
if (
  !is.finite(remainder_scale) ||
  remainder_scale == 0
) {
  remainder_scale <- sd(
    air_components$Remainder,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
}

air_components <- air_components |>
  mutate(
    Remainder_robust_z =
      (Remainder - remainder_center) /
      remainder_scale,
    Unusual_remainder =
      abs(Remainder_robust_z) > 2.5
  )

# Data for highlighted remainder observations
unusual_remainders <- air_components |>
  filter(Unusual_remainder) |>
  transmute(
    Date = Date,
    Value = Remainder,
    Component = factor(
      "Remainder component: Rt",
      levels = levels(
        air_components_long$Component
      )
    )
  )

# Select up to two unusual observations for labels
remainder_labels <- unusual_remainders |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = abs(Value),
    n = min(
      2L,
      nrow(unusual_remainders)
    ),
    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Label = format(
      Date,
      "%b %Y"
    ),
    Label_y = if_else(
      Value >= 0,
      Value + 0.025,
      Value - 0.025
    ),
    Vjust = if_else(
      Value >= 0,
      0,
      1
    )
  )

# Colors for the four components
component_colors <- c(
  "Observed" = "#173F73",
  "Trend" = "#059669",
  "Seasonal" = "#7C3AED",
  "Remainder" = "#64748B"
)

# Build the decomposition figure
decomposition_plot <- ggplot(
  data = air_components_long,
  aes(
    x = Date,
    y = Value,
    color = Component_code,
    group = Component
  )
) +
  geom_hline(
    data = zero_lines,
    aes(
      yintercept = Reference
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#CBD5E1",
    linewidth = 0.55
  ) +
  geom_line(
    linewidth = 0.9,
    lineend = "round"
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = unusual_remainders,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Value
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#DC2626",
    fill = "white",
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.2,
    stroke = 1.2
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = remainder_labels,
    aes(
      x = Date,
      y = Label_y,
      label = Label,
      vjust = Vjust
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#B91C1C",
    size = 2.7,
    fontface = "bold",
    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(Component),
    scales = "free_y",
    switch = "y",
    labeller = label_value
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = component_colors,
    guide = "none"
  ) +
  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "2 years",
    date_minor_breaks = "1 year",
    date_labels = "%Y",
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.01, 0.025)
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    labels = label_number(
      accuracy = 0.01
    ),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0.15, 0.18)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Decomposing the AirPassengers Time Series",
    subtitle = paste0(
      "Additive STL decomposition on the log scale: ",
      "Yt = Tt + St + Rt"
    ),
    x = "Year",
    y = NULL,
    caption = paste0(
      "The logarithmic transformation stabilizes the increasing ",
      "seasonal amplitude. Red circles identify unusually large ",
      "remainder values using a robust standardized threshold."
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 13
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#172033",
      margin = margin(b = 4)
    ),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 12.5,
      color = "#475569",
      margin = margin(b = 12)
    ),
    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 8.5,
      color = "#64748B",
      hjust = 0,
      lineheight = 1.15,
      margin = margin(t = 10)
    ),
    strip.placement = "outside",
    strip.background = element_rect(
      fill = "#F8FAFC",
      color = "#CBD5E1",
      linewidth = 0.5
    ),
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      size = 9.5,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#334155",
      hjust = 0.5,
      margin = margin(
        t = 6,
        r = 9,
        b = 6,
        l = 9
      )
    ),
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 11,
      face = "bold",
      color = "#334155",
      margin = margin(t = 8)
    ),
    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 8.5,
      color = "#64748B"
    ),
    axis.ticks = element_line(
      color = "#CBD5E1",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(
      color = "#E5E7EB",
      linewidth = 0.4
    ),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(
      color = "#F1F5F9",
      linewidth = 0.35
    ),
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_line(
      color = "#F1F5F9",
      linewidth = 0.25
    ),
    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(
      0.45,
      "lines"
    ),
    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 24,
      b = 8,
      l = 10
    )
  )

decomposition_plot
```


::: {.notes}

A trend exists when there is a long-term increase or decrease in the data. It does not have to be linear. Sometimes we will refer to a trend as “changing direction”, when it might go from an increasing trend to a decreasing trend.

A seasonal pattern occurs when a time series is affected by seasonal factors such as the time of the year or the day of the week. Seasonality is always of a fixed and known period.

A cycle occurs when the data exhibit rises and falls that are not of a fixed frequency. These fluctuations are usually due to economic conditions, and are often related to the “business cycle”. The duration of these fluctuations is usually at least 2 years.

:::

## Time Series Decomposition

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ================================================================
# 1. VALIDATE THE MONTHLY DATASET
# ================================================================

required_columns <- c(
  "ticker",
  "month",
  "monthly_adjusted_price"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(monthly_data)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The following columns are missing from monthly_data: ",
      paste(
        missing_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 2. SELECT THE FIRST VALID TICKER
# ================================================================

ticker_selected <- monthly_data |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ticker),
    as.character(ticker) != ""
  ) |>
  distinct(ticker) |>
  slice_head(n = 1L) |>
  pull(ticker) |>
  as.character()

if (
  length(ticker_selected) == 0L ||
  is.na(ticker_selected)
) {
  stop(
    "No valid ticker was found in monthly_data."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 3. PREPARE THE MONTHLY ADJUSTED-PRICE SERIES
# ================================================================

monthly_trend_data <- monthly_data |>
  filter(
    ticker == ticker_selected
  ) |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker),

    month = as.Date(month),

    monthly_adjusted_price =
      suppressWarnings(
        as.numeric(
          monthly_adjusted_price
        )
      )
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(month),
    is.finite(monthly_adjusted_price)
  ) |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    month
  ) |>
  summarise(
    monthly_adjusted_price = last(
      monthly_adjusted_price
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(month)

n_months <- nrow(
  monthly_trend_data
)

if (n_months < 13L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least 13 monthly prices are required. ",
      "Only ",
      n_months,
      " were found for ",
      ticker_selected,
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 4. VERIFY THAT THE SERIES HAS NO MISSING CALENDAR MONTHS
#
# Classical decomposition assumes equally spaced observations.
# ================================================================

expected_months <- seq.Date(
  from = min(
    monthly_trend_data$month
  ),

  to = max(
    monthly_trend_data$month
  ),

  by = "month"
)

observed_months <- monthly_trend_data$month

missing_months <- expected_months[
  !expected_months %in%
    observed_months
]

if (length(missing_months) > 0L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The monthly series contains missing calendar months: ",
      paste(
        format(
          missing_months,
          "%b %Y"
        ),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      ". Treat the missing months before estimating the trend."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 5. DEFINE THE CENTERED 2 x 12 MOVING-AVERAGE WEIGHTS
#
# For monthly data, m = 12.
#
# Because 12 is even, the centered moving average is equivalent
# to a 13-term weighted moving average:
#
# 1/24, 1/12, ..., 1/12, 1/24
# ================================================================

trend_weights <- c(
  1 / 24,

  rep(
    1 / 12,
    11L
  ),

  1 / 24
)

stopifnot(
  length(trend_weights) == 13L,

  isTRUE(
    all.equal(
      sum(trend_weights),
      1
    )
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 6. ESTIMATE THE CLASSICAL MONTHLY TREND
#
# T_hat(t) =
# Y_(t-6)/24
# + sum[Y_(t+j)/12], j = -5,...,5
# + Y_(t+6)/24
# ================================================================

monthly_trend_data <- monthly_trend_data |>
  mutate(
    classical_trend = as.numeric(
      stats::filter(
        x = monthly_adjusted_price,

        filter = trend_weights,

        sides = 2
      )
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 7. RETAIN VALID TREND ESTIMATES
#
# Six observations are lost at each edge because the estimate
# requires six months before and six months after time t.
# ================================================================

valid_trend_data <- monthly_trend_data |>
  filter(
    !is.na(classical_trend),
    is.finite(classical_trend)
  )

expected_trend_count <-
  n_months - 12L

if (
  nrow(valid_trend_data) !=
    expected_trend_count
) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Unexpected number of trend estimates. Expected ",
      expected_trend_count,
      " but obtained ",
      nrow(valid_trend_data),
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 8. SELECT ONE COMPLETE 13-MONTH WINDOW FOR ILLUSTRATION
# ================================================================

valid_indices <- which(
  is.finite(
    monthly_trend_data$classical_trend
  )
)

example_center_index <- valid_indices[
  ceiling(
    length(valid_indices) / 2
  )
]

example_window_indices <- seq.int(
  from = example_center_index - 6L,

  to = example_center_index + 6L
)

example_window <- monthly_trend_data[
  example_window_indices,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

example_center <- monthly_trend_data[
  example_center_index,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

# ================================================================
# 9. VALIDATE THE EXAMPLE MANUALLY
# ================================================================

manual_example_trend <- sum(
  example_window$monthly_adjusted_price *
    trend_weights
)

filter_example_trend <-
  example_center$classical_trend[1]

if (
  !isTRUE(
    all.equal(
      manual_example_trend,
      filter_example_trend,
      tolerance = 1e-10
    )
  )
) {
  stop(
    "The manual trend estimate does not match the filtered estimate."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 10. PREPARE THE HIGHLIGHTED WINDOW
# ================================================================

window_region <- data.frame(
  xmin = min(
    example_window$month
  ),

  xmax = max(
    example_window$month
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 11. CREATE FORMATTING AND LABELS
# ================================================================

median_price <- median(
  monthly_trend_data$monthly_adjusted_price,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

price_accuracy <- if (
  median_price >= 100
) {
  1
} else if (
  median_price >= 10
) {
  0.1
} else {
  0.01
}

format_price <- label_number(
  accuracy = price_accuracy,
  big.mark = ","
)

price_range <- diff(
  range(
    monthly_trend_data$monthly_adjusted_price,
    na.rm = TRUE
  )
)

if (
  !is.finite(price_range) ||
  price_range <= 0
) {
  price_range <- 1
}

label_y <-
  filter_example_trend +
  0.15 * price_range

trend_label <- paste0(
  "Centered 2 × 12 moving average\n",
  format(
    example_center$month[1],
    "%b %Y"
  ),
  "\n",
  "Estimated trend = ",
  format_price(
    filter_example_trend
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 12. CREATE THE FIGURE
# ================================================================

monthly_trend_plot <- ggplot(
  data = monthly_trend_data,

  aes(
    x = month
  )
) +

  # Highlight one centered 13-month window

  geom_rect(

    ),
```
