## Time Series Decomposition

```{r}
# ================================================================
# DETRENDED MONTHLY ADJUSTED-PRICE SERIES
# Classical decomposition with a centered 2 x 12 moving average
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ================================================================
# 1. VALIDATE THE INPUT DATASET
#
# This code assumes that monthly_data was created previously
# and contains one or more tickers with monthly adjusted prices.
# ================================================================

if (!exists("monthly_data")) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The object 'monthly_data' does not exist. ",
      "Create the monthly adjusted-price dataset before running ",
      "this chunk."
    )
  )
}

required_columns <- c(
  "ticker",
  "month",
  "monthly_adjusted_price"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(monthly_data)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The following required columns are missing from monthly_data: ",
      paste(
        missing_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 2. SELECT THE FIRST VALID TICKER
# ================================================================

available_tickers <- monthly_data |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker)
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ticker),
    ticker != ""
  ) |>
  distinct(ticker) |>
  pull(ticker)

if (length(available_tickers) == 0L) {
  stop(
    "No valid ticker was found in monthly_data."
  )
}

ticker_selected <- available_tickers[1]

# ================================================================
# 3. PREPARE THE MONTHLY ADJUSTED-PRICE SERIES
#
# The code guarantees one price for each ticker-month pair.
# If duplicates exist, the final finite value is retained.
# ================================================================

monthly_price_series <- monthly_data |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker),

    month = as.Date(month),

    monthly_adjusted_price = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(
        monthly_adjusted_price
      )
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    ticker == ticker_selected,
    !is.na(month),
    is.finite(monthly_adjusted_price)
  ) |>
  arrange(
    month
  ) |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    month
  ) |>
  summarise(
    monthly_adjusted_price = last(
      monthly_adjusted_price
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(
    month
  )

n_months <- nrow(
  monthly_price_series
)

if (n_months < 13L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least 13 monthly observations are required to calculate ",
      "a centered 2 x 12 moving average. Only ",
      n_months,
      " were found for ",
      ticker_selected,
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 4. CHECK THE MONTHLY FREQUENCY
#
# Classical decomposition assumes an equally spaced monthly series.
# ================================================================

expected_month_sequence <- seq.Date(
  from = min(
    monthly_price_series$month
  ),

  to = max(
    monthly_price_series$month
  ),

  by = "month"
)

missing_months <- expected_month_sequence[
  !expected_month_sequence %in%
    monthly_price_series$month
]

if (length(missing_months) > 0L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The series contains missing calendar months: ",
      paste(
        format(
          missing_months,
          "%b %Y"
        ),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      ". Classical decomposition requires an equally spaced series."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 5. DEFINE THE CENTERED 2 x 12 MOVING-AVERAGE WEIGHTS
#
# With monthly data, the seasonal period is m = 12.
#
# Since m is even, the centered trend is obtained from a
# 13-observation weighted moving average:
#
#            1      5             1
# T_hat_t = ---Y_t-6 + sum ---Y_t+j + ---Y_t+6
#           24     j=-5 12        24
# ================================================================

trend_weights <- c(
  1 / 24,

  rep(
    1 / 12,
    times = 11L
  ),

  1 / 24
)

if (length(trend_weights) != 13L) {
  stop(
    "The centered moving-average filter must contain 13 weights."
  )
}

if (
  !isTRUE(
    all.equal(
      sum(trend_weights),
      1,
      tolerance = 1e-12
    )
  )
) {
  stop(
    "The centered moving-average weights do not sum to one."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 6. ESTIMATE THE CLASSICAL TREND
#
# stats::filter(..., sides = 2) applies the weights symmetrically.
# Six months before and six months after t are required.
# ================================================================

estimated_trend <- as.numeric(
  stats::filter(
    x = monthly_price_series$monthly_adjusted_price,

    filter = trend_weights,

    sides = 2
  )
)

monthly_price_series <- monthly_price_series |>
  mutate(
    estimated_trend = estimated_trend
  )

# ================================================================
# 7. CALCULATE THE DETRENDED SERIES
#
# D_t = Y_t - T_hat_t
#
# For the classical additive decomposition:
#
# D_t = S_t + R_t
# ================================================================

monthly_price_series <- monthly_price_series |>
  mutate(
    detrended_price =
      monthly_adjusted_price -
      estimated_trend
  )

# ================================================================
# 8. RETAIN DATES WITH VALID CENTERED TREND ESTIMATES
#
# The first and final six months do not have trend estimates.
# ================================================================

detrended_data <- monthly_price_series |>
  filter(
    is.finite(estimated_trend),
    is.finite(detrended_price)
  )

n_detrended_observations <- nrow(
  detrended_data
)

expected_detrended_observations <-
  n_months - 12L

if (
  n_detrended_observations !=
    expected_detrended_observations
) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Unexpected number of detrended observations. Expected ",
      expected_detrended_observations,
      " but obtained ",
      n_detrended_observations,
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 9. VALIDATE THE DETRENDING IDENTITY
#
# Wherever the trend is available:
#
# Y_t = T_hat_t + D_t
# ================================================================

reconstruction_error <- max(
  abs(
    detrended_data$monthly_adjusted_price -
      (
        detrended_data$estimated_trend +
          detrended_data$detrended_price
      )
  ),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(reconstruction_error) ||
  reconstruction_error > 1e-10
) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The detrending identity failed. Maximum reconstruction error: ",
      format(
        reconstruction_error,
        scientific = TRUE
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 10. CLASSIFY VALUES RELATIVE TO THE TREND
# ================================================================

detrended_data <- detrended_data |>
  mutate(
    position_relative_to_trend = case_when(
      detrended_price > 0 ~
        "Price above trend",

      detrended_price < 0 ~
        "Price below trend",

      TRUE ~
        "Price equal to trend"
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 11. CALCULATE DESCRIPTIVE STATISTICS
# ================================================================

mean_detrended <- mean(
  detrended_data$detrended_price,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

sd_detrended <- sd(
  detrended_data$detrended_price,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

maximum_detrended <- max(
  detrended_data$detrended_price,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

minimum_detrended <- min(
  detrended_data$detrended_price,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

# ================================================================
# 12. IDENTIFY LARGE ABSOLUTE DEVIATIONS
#
# The largest 5% are emphasized only as a visualization device.
# This is not presented as a formal outlier-detection rule.
# ================================================================

large_deviation_threshold <- quantile(
  abs(
    detrended_data$detrended_price
  ),

  probs = 0.95,

  names = FALSE,

  na.rm = TRUE,

  type = 7
)

detrended_data <- detrended_data |>
  mutate(
    deviation_class = if_else(
      abs(detrended_price) >=
        large_deviation_threshold,

      "Large absolute deviation",

      "Regular deviation"
    )
  )

regular_deviations <- detrended_data |>
  filter(
    deviation_class ==
      "Regular deviation"
  )

large_deviations <- detrended_data |>
  filter(
    deviation_class ==
      "Large absolute deviation"
  )

# ================================================================
# 13. IDENTIFY THE LARGEST POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE DEVIATIONS
# ================================================================

largest_positive_deviation <- detrended_data |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = detrended_price,

    n = 1L,

    with_ties = FALSE
  )

largest_negative_deviation <- detrended_data |>
  slice_min(
    order_by = detrended_price,

    n = 1L,

    with_ties = FALSE
  )

extreme_deviations <- bind_rows(
  largest_positive_deviation,
  largest_negative_deviation
) |>
  distinct(
    month,

    .keep_all = TRUE
  )

# ================================================================
# 14. DEFINE THE NUMBER FORMAT
#
# Detrended values retain the price unit.
# ================================================================

median_price <- median(
  detrended_data$monthly_adjusted_price,

  na.rm = TRUE
)

price_accuracy <- if (
  median_price >= 100
) {
  1
} else if (
  median_price >= 10
) {
  0.1
} else {
  0.01
}

price_formatter <- label_number(
  accuracy = price_accuracy,

  big.mark = ","
)

# ================================================================
# 15. CREATE LABELS FOR EXTREME DEVIATIONS
# ================================================================

extreme_deviations <- extreme_deviations |>
  mutate(
    extreme_label = paste0(
      format(
        month,
        "%b %Y"
      ),
      "\n",
      if_else(
        detrended_price > 0,
        "Above trend: ",
        "Below trend: "
      ),
      price_formatter(
        detrended_price
      )
    ),

    vertical_justification = if_else(
      detrended_price >= 0,

      -0.75,

      1.65
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 16. CREATE A SYMMETRIC VERTICAL SCALE
#
# A symmetric scale makes positive and negative deviations directly
# comparable.
# ================================================================

maximum_absolute_deviation <- max(
  abs(
    detrended_data$detrended_price
  ),

  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(maximum_absolute_deviation) ||
  maximum_absolute_deviation <= 0
) {
  maximum_absolute_deviation <- 1
}

vertical_limit <-
  1.22 *
  maximum_absolute_deviation

# ================================================================
# 17. CREATE LABEL POSITIONS FOR EXPLANATORY TEXT
# ================================================================

first_valid_month <- min(
  detrended_data$month
)

last_valid_month <- max(
  detrended_data$month
)

positive_region_y <-
  0.78 *
  vertical_limit

negative_region_y <-
  -0.78 *
  vertical_limit

# ================================================================
# 18. CREATE THE DETRENDED-SERIES FIGURE
# ================================================================

monthly_detrended_plot <- ggplot(
  data = detrended_data,

  aes(
    x = month,
    y = detrended_price
  )
) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Positive-deviation area
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = 0,

      ymax = ifelse(
        detrended_price > 0,
        detrended_price,
        0
      )
    ),

    fill = "#2F6FA5",

    alpha = 0.15
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Negative-deviation area
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = ifelse(
        detrended_price < 0,
        detrended_price,
        0
      ),

      ymax = 0
    ),

    fill = "#DC2626",

    alpha = 0.15
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Zero-reference line
  #
  # At zero:
  #
  # observed price = estimated trend
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,

    color = "#334155",

    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Complete detrended series
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    color = "#64748B",

    linewidth = 0.7,

    alpha = 0.80,

    lineend = "round"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Regular observations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = regular_deviations,

    aes(
      x = month,
      y = detrended_price,
      color = position_relative_to_trend
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    size = 2,

    alpha = 0.62
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Large absolute deviations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = large_deviations,

    aes(
      x = month,
      y = detrended_price
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#D97706",

    fill = "white",

    shape = 21,

    size = 3.5,

    stroke = 1.1
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Label the largest positive and negative deviations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_text(
    data = extreme_deviations,

    aes(
      x = month,
      y = detrended_price,
      label = extreme_label,
      vjust = vertical_justification
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#334155",

    size = 2.9,

    fontface = "bold",

    lineheight = 0.95,

    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Explain the positive region
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  annotate(
    geom = "label",

    x = first_valid_month,

    y = positive_region_y,

    label = paste0(
      "D(t) > 0\n",
      "Price above trend"
    ),

    hjust = 0,

    color = "#1D4ED8",

    fill = "white",

    fontface = "bold",

    size = 3,

    lineheight = 1,

    label.size = 0.25
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Explain the negative region
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  annotate(
    geom = "label",

    x = first_valid_month,

    y = negative_region_y,

    label = paste0(
      "D(t) < 0\n",
      "Price below trend"
    ),

    hjust = 0,

    color = "#B91C1C",

    fill = "white",

    fontface = "bold",

    size = 3,

    lineheight = 1,

    label.size = 0.25
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Colors
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,

    values = c(
      "Price above trend" =
        "#2F6FA5",

      "Price below trend" =
        "#DC2626",

      "Price equal to trend" =
        "#059669"
    ),

    breaks = c(
      "Price above trend",
      "Price below trend",
      "Price equal to trend"
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Horizontal scale
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 year",

    date_minor_breaks = "3 months",

    date_labels = "%Y",

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.01,
        0.02
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Symmetric vertical scale
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      -vertical_limit,

    ),

    labels = price_formatter,

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0,
        0
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Titles
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  labs(

      "What Remains After Removing the Monthly Trend?",

    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(

  ) +

  theme(
```

## Time Series Decomposition

```{r}
# ================================================================
# CLASSICAL SEASONAL COMPONENT
# Monthly adjusted prices
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ================================================================
# 1. VALIDATE THE MONTHLY DATA
# ================================================================

if (!exists("monthly_data")) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The object 'monthly_data' does not exist. ",
      "Run the daily-to-monthly aggregation code first."
    )
  )
}

required_columns <- c(
  "ticker",
  "month",
  "monthly_adjusted_price"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(monthly_data)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The following columns are missing from monthly_data: ",
      paste(
        missing_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 2. SELECT THE FIRST VALID TICKER
# ================================================================

ticker_selected <- monthly_data |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ticker),
    as.character(ticker) != ""
  ) |>
  distinct(ticker) |>
  slice_head(n = 1L) |>
  pull(ticker) |>
  as.character()

if (
  length(ticker_selected) == 0L ||
  is.na(ticker_selected)
) {
  stop(
    "No valid ticker was found in monthly_data."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 3. PREPARE ONE PRICE PER CALENDAR MONTH
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_data |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker),

    month = as.Date(month),

    monthly_adjusted_price = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(
        monthly_adjusted_price
      )
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    ticker == ticker_selected,
    !is.na(month),
    is.finite(monthly_adjusted_price)
  ) |>
  arrange(month) |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    month
  ) |>
  summarise(
    monthly_adjusted_price = last(
      monthly_adjusted_price
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(month)

n_months <- nrow(
  monthly_series
)

if (n_months < 24L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least 24 monthly observations are required. ",
      "Only ",
      n_months,
      " observations were found for ",
      ticker_selected,
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 4. CHECK FOR DUPLICATED MONTHS
# ================================================================

duplicated_months <- monthly_series |>
  count(month) |>
  filter(n > 1L)

if (nrow(duplicated_months) > 0L) {
  stop(
    "The monthly series contains duplicated months."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 5. CHECK FOR MISSING CALENDAR MONTHS
#
# Classical decomposition requires equally spaced observations.
# ================================================================

expected_months <- seq.Date(
  from = min(
    monthly_series$month
  ),

  to = max(
    monthly_series$month
  ),

  by = "month"
)

missing_months <- expected_months[
  !expected_months %in%
    monthly_series$month
]

if (length(missing_months) > 0L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The series contains missing calendar months: ",
      paste(
        format(
          missing_months,
          "%b %Y"
        ),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      ". Complete or treat the missing months before ",
      "applying classical decomposition."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 6. CREATE THE MONTHLY TIME-SERIES OBJECT
#
# frequency = 12 defines an annual seasonal cycle.
# ================================================================

start_year <- as.integer(
  format(
    min(monthly_series$month),
    "%Y"
  )
)

start_month <- as.integer(
  format(
    min(monthly_series$month),
    "%m"
  )
)

monthly_price_ts <- ts(
  data = monthly_series$monthly_adjusted_price,

  start = c(
    start_year,
    start_month
  ),

  frequency = 12
)

# ================================================================
# 7. APPLY CLASSICAL ADDITIVE DECOMPOSITION
#
# Y_t = T_t + S_t + R_t
#
# stats::decompose() estimates:
# - trend with a centered moving average;
# - seasonal effects from detrended monthly values;
# - remainder by subtraction.
# ================================================================

classical_decomposition <- stats::decompose(
  x = monthly_price_ts,

  type = "additive"
)

# ================================================================
# 8. EXTRACT THE COMPONENTS
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_series |>
  mutate(
    observed_price = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$x
    ),

    trend_component = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$trend
    ),

    seasonal_component = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$seasonal
    ),

    remainder_component = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$random
    ),

    calendar_month_number = as.integer(
      format(
        month,
        "%m"
      )
    ),

    calendar_month = factor(
      calendar_month_number,

      levels = 1:12,

      labels = month.abb,

      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 9. VALIDATE THE SEASONAL COMPONENT
# ================================================================

if (
  any(
    !is.finite(
      monthly_series$seasonal_component
    )
  )
) {
  stop(
    "The classical decomposition produced invalid seasonal values."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 10. EXTRACT THE 12 UNIQUE SEASONAL INDICES
#
# Classical decomposition estimates one effect for each month
# and repeats the same 12-month pattern every year.
# ================================================================

seasonal_indices <- monthly_series |>
  group_by(
    calendar_month_number,
    calendar_month
  ) |>
  summarise(
    seasonal_effect = mean(
      seasonal_component,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(
    calendar_month_number
  )

if (nrow(seasonal_indices) != 12L) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "Expected 12 seasonal indices, but obtained ",
      nrow(seasonal_indices),
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 11. VALIDATE THE ADDITIVE CENTERING CONSTRAINT
#
# The 12 monthly seasonal effects must sum to approximately zero.
# ================================================================

sum_seasonal_effects <- sum(
  seasonal_indices$seasonal_effect
)

if (
  !isTRUE(
    all.equal(
      sum_seasonal_effects,
      0,
      tolerance = 1e-8
    )
  )
) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The seasonal effects do not sum to zero. ",
      "Calculated sum: ",
      format(
        sum_seasonal_effects,
        scientific = TRUE
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 12. VALIDATE THE ADDITIVE DECOMPOSITION
#
# For dates where trend and remainder are available:
#
# Y_t = T_t + S_t + R_t
# ================================================================

complete_components <- monthly_series |>
  filter(
    is.finite(trend_component),
    is.finite(seasonal_component),
    is.finite(remainder_component)
  )

reconstruction_error <- max(
  abs(
    complete_components$observed_price -
      (
        complete_components$trend_component +
        complete_components$seasonal_component +
        complete_components$remainder_component
      )
  ),
  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(reconstruction_error) ||
  reconstruction_error > 1e-8
) {
  stop(
    paste0(
      "The additive decomposition identity failed. ",
      "Maximum reconstruction error: ",
      format(
        reconstruction_error,
        scientific = TRUE
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 13. CLASSIFY POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE SEASONAL EFFECTS
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_series |>
  mutate(
    seasonal_direction = case_when(
      seasonal_component > 0 ~
        "Raises price relative to trend",

      seasonal_component < 0 ~
        "Lowers price relative to trend",

      TRUE ~
        "No seasonal effect"
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 14. PREPARE POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE AREA VALUES
#
# These columns ensure that geom_ribbon() draws the positive and
# negative regions correctly.
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_series |>
  mutate(
    positive_seasonal = if_else(
      seasonal_component > 0,

      seasonal_component,

      0
    ),

    negative_seasonal = if_else(
      seasonal_component < 0,

      seasonal_component,

      0
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 15. IDENTIFY THE LARGEST POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE EFFECTS
#
# The seasonal pattern repeats every year. The final occurrence
# of the highest and lowest seasonal months is highlighted.
# ================================================================

highest_month_number <- seasonal_indices |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = seasonal_effect,

    n = 1L,

    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  pull(
    calendar_month_number
  )

lowest_month_number <- seasonal_indices |>
  slice_min(
    order_by = seasonal_effect,

    n = 1L,

    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  pull(
    calendar_month_number
  )

highest_effect_point <- monthly_series |>
  filter(
    calendar_month_number ==
      highest_month_number
  ) |>
  slice_tail(
    n = 1L
  )

lowest_effect_point <- monthly_series |>
  filter(
    calendar_month_number ==
      lowest_month_number
  ) |>
  slice_tail(
    n = 1L
  )

highlight_points <- bind_rows(
  highest_effect_point,
  lowest_effect_point
)

# ================================================================
# 16. DEFINE THE PRICE FORMAT
#
# Seasonal effects are expressed in the original price unit.
# ================================================================

median_price <- median(
  monthly_series$monthly_adjusted_price,

  na.rm = TRUE
)

price_accuracy <- if (
  median_price >= 100
) {
  1
} else if (
  median_price >= 10
) {
  0.1
} else {
  0.01
}

price_formatter <- label_number(
  accuracy = price_accuracy,

  big.mark = ","
)

# ================================================================
# 17. CREATE HIGHLIGHT LABELS
# ================================================================

highlight_points <- highlight_points |>
  mutate(
    label = paste0(
      as.character(
        calendar_month
      ),
      " seasonal effect\n",
      if_else(
        seasonal_component > 0,
        "+",
        ""
      ),
      price_formatter(
        seasonal_component
      )
    ),

    vertical_justification = if_else(
      seasonal_component > 0,

      -0.8,

      1.8
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 18. DEFINE A SYMMETRIC VERTICAL SCALE
# ================================================================

maximum_absolute_effect <- max(
  abs(
    monthly_series$seasonal_component
  ),

  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(maximum_absolute_effect) ||
  maximum_absolute_effect <= 0
) {
  maximum_absolute_effect <- 1
}

vertical_limit <- 1.30 *
  maximum_absolute_effect

# ================================================================
# 19. CREATE THE SEASONAL-COMPONENT TIME-SERIES PLOT
# ================================================================

seasonal_component_plot <- ggplot(
  data = monthly_series,

  aes(
    x = month,
    y = seasonal_component
  )
) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Positive seasonal region
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = 0,
      ymax = positive_seasonal
    ),

    fill = "#2F6FA5",

    alpha = 0.17
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Negative seasonal region
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = negative_seasonal,
      ymax = 0
    ),

    fill = "#DC2626",

    alpha = 0.17
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Zero reference
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,

    color = "#334155",

    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Seasonal component through time
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    color = "#64748B",

    linewidth = 0.75,

    alpha = 0.88,

    lineend = "round"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Monthly seasonal observations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    aes(
      color = seasonal_direction
    ),

    size = 2,

    alpha = 0.72
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Highlight the strongest positive and negative months
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = highlight_points,

    aes(
      x = month,
      y = seasonal_component
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#D97706",

    fill = "white",

    shape = 21,

    size = 4,

    stroke = 1.15
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Label the highlighted seasonal effects
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_text(
    data = highlight_points,

    aes(
      x = month,
      y = seasonal_component,
      label = label,
      vjust = vertical_justification
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#334155",

    size = 3,

    fontface = "bold",

    lineheight = 0.95,

    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Point colors
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,

    values = c(
      "Raises price relative to trend" =
        "#2F6FA5",

      "Lowers price relative to trend" =
        "#DC2626",

      "No seasonal effect" =
        "#059669"
    ),

    breaks = c(
      "Raises price relative to trend",
      "Lowers price relative to trend",
      "No seasonal effect"
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Time axis
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 year",

    date_minor_breaks = "3 months",

    date_labels = "%Y",

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.01,
        0.02
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Seasonal-effect axis
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      -vertical_limit,
      vertical_limit
    ),

    labels = price_formatter,

    breaks = pretty_breaks(
      n = 5
    ),

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0,
        0
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Titles
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  labs(
    title =
      "How Does Seasonality Raise or Lower Monthly Price?",

    subtitle = paste0(
      ticker_selected,
      " monthly adjusted prices | ",
      "Classical additive seasonal component"
    ),

    x = "Month",

    y = expression(
      hat(S)[t]
    ),

    caption = paste0(
      "The seasonal component repeats the same 12 monthly effects ",
      "in each year. Blue values raise price relative to the trend; ",
      "red values lower it. The 12 unique seasonal effects sum to zero."
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Presentation theme
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 13
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,

      face = "bold",

      color = "#172033",

      margin = margin(
        b = 4
      )
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11.5,

      color = "#475569",

      margin = margin(
        b = 13
      )
    ),

    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 8.5,

      color = "#64748B",

      hjust = 0,

      lineheight = 1.15,

      margin = margin(
        t = 10
      )
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 11,

      face = "bold",

      color = "#334155"
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 8.5,

      color = "#64748B"
    ),

    panel.grid.major = element_line(
      color = "#E5E7EB",

      linewidth = 0.4
    ),

    panel.grid.minor.x = element_line(
      color = "#F1F5F9",

      linewidth = 0.25
    ),

    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),

    legend.position = "bottom",

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 9.5,

      color = "#475569"
    ),

    legend.key.width = grid::unit(
      0.9,
      "cm"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 20,
      b = 8,
      l = 10
    )
  ) +

  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        size = 3,

        alpha = 0.9
      )
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 20. DISPLAY THE FIGURE
# ================================================================

seasonal_component_plot
```

## Time Series Decomposition

```{r}
#| label: seasonally-adjusted-monthly-price
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| fig-width: 12
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| dpi: 300

# ================================================================
# SEASONALLY ADJUSTED MONTHLY PRICE SERIES
# Classical additive decomposition
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ================================================================
# 1. VALIDATE THE INPUT DATASET
# ================================================================

if (!exists("monthly_data")) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The object 'monthly_data' does not exist. ",
      "Create the monthly adjusted-price dataset before ",
      "running this chunk."
    )
  )
}

required_columns <- c(
  "ticker",
  "month",
  "monthly_adjusted_price"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(monthly_data)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The following required columns are missing from monthly_data: ",
      paste(
        missing_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 2. SELECT THE FIRST VALID TICKER
# ================================================================

available_tickers <- monthly_data |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker)
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ticker),
    ticker != ""
  ) |>
  distinct(ticker) |>
  pull(ticker)

if (length(available_tickers) == 0L) {

  stop(
    "No valid ticker was found in monthly_data."
  )
}

ticker_selected <- available_tickers[1]

# ================================================================
# 3. PREPARE ONE ADJUSTED PRICE PER MONTH
#
# If duplicate ticker-month observations exist, the final finite
# price is retained.
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_data |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker),

    month = as.Date(month),

    monthly_adjusted_price = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(
        monthly_adjusted_price
      )
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    ticker == ticker_selected,
    !is.na(month),
    is.finite(monthly_adjusted_price)
  ) |>
  arrange(month) |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    month
  ) |>
  summarise(
    monthly_adjusted_price = last(
      monthly_adjusted_price
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(month)

n_months <- nrow(
  monthly_series
)

if (n_months < 24L) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least 24 monthly observations are required for a ",
      "meaningful annual seasonal decomposition. Only ",
      n_months,
      " were found for ",
      ticker_selected,
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 4. CHECK FOR DUPLICATED MONTHS
# ================================================================

duplicated_months <- monthly_series |>
  count(month) |>
  filter(
    n > 1L
  )

if (nrow(duplicated_months) > 0L) {

  stop(
    "The monthly price series contains duplicated months."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 5. CHECK FOR MISSING CALENDAR MONTHS
#
# Classical decomposition requires regularly spaced observations.
# ================================================================

expected_month_sequence <- seq.Date(
  from = min(
    monthly_series$month
  ),

  to = max(
    monthly_series$month
  ),

  by = "month"
)

missing_calendar_months <- expected_month_sequence[
  !expected_month_sequence %in%
    monthly_series$month
]

if (length(missing_calendar_months) > 0L) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The monthly series contains missing calendar months: ",
      paste(
        format(
          missing_calendar_months,
          "%b %Y"
        ),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      ". Treat the missing months before applying classical ",
      "decomposition."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 6. CREATE THE MONTHLY TIME-SERIES OBJECT
#
# frequency = 12 defines an annual seasonal cycle.
# ================================================================

first_year <- as.integer(
  format(
    min(monthly_series$month),
    "%Y"
  )
)

first_month <- as.integer(
  format(
    min(monthly_series$month),
    "%m"
  )
)

monthly_price_ts <- stats::ts(
  data = monthly_series$monthly_adjusted_price,

  start = c(
    first_year,
    first_month
  ),

  frequency = 12
)

# ================================================================
# 7. APPLY CLASSICAL ADDITIVE DECOMPOSITION
#
# Y_t = T_t + S_t + R_t
#
# stats::decompose() estimates:
#
# - trend using a centered 2 x 12 moving average;
# - seasonality by averaging detrended values by month;
# - remainder by subtraction.
# ================================================================

classical_decomposition <- stats::decompose(
  x = monthly_price_ts,

  type = "additive"
)

# ================================================================
# 8. EXTRACT THE COMPONENTS
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_series |>
  mutate(
    observed_price = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$x
    ),

    trend_component = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$trend
    ),

    seasonal_component = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$seasonal
    ),

    remainder_component = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$random
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 9. CALCULATE THE SEASONALLY ADJUSTED SERIES
#
# For an additive decomposition:
#
# Y_t^(SA) = Y_t - S_t
#
# Therefore:
#
# Y_t^(SA) = T_t + R_t
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_series |>
  mutate(
    seasonally_adjusted_price =
      observed_price -
      seasonal_component
  )

# ================================================================
# 10. VALIDATE THE SEASONAL ADJUSTMENT
# ================================================================

if (
  any(
    !is.finite(
      monthly_series$seasonal_component
    )
  )
) {

  stop(
    "The decomposition produced invalid seasonal-component values."
  )
}

if (
  any(
    !is.finite(
      monthly_series$seasonally_adjusted_price
    )
  )
) {

  stop(
    "The seasonally adjusted series contains invalid values."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 11. EXTRACT THE 12 UNIQUE SEASONAL INDICES
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_series |>
  mutate(
    calendar_month_number = as.integer(
      format(
        month,
        "%m"
      )
    ),

    calendar_month = factor(
      calendar_month_number,

      levels = 1:12,

      labels = month.abb,

      ordered = TRUE
    )
  )

seasonal_indices <- monthly_series |>
  group_by(
    calendar_month_number,
    calendar_month
  ) |>
  summarise(
    seasonal_effect = mean(
      seasonal_component,
      na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(
    calendar_month_number
  )

if (nrow(seasonal_indices) != 12L) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Expected 12 seasonal effects, but obtained ",
      nrow(seasonal_indices),
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 12. VALIDATE THAT THE SEASONAL INDICES SUM TO ZERO
# ================================================================

sum_of_seasonal_effects <- sum(
  seasonal_indices$seasonal_effect
)

if (
  !isTRUE(
    all.equal(
      sum_of_seasonal_effects,
      0,
      tolerance = 1e-8
    )
  )
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The additive seasonal effects do not sum to zero. ",
      "Calculated sum: ",
      format(
        sum_of_seasonal_effects,
        scientific = TRUE
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 13. VALIDATE THE SEASONAL-ADJUSTMENT IDENTITY
#
# Observed price =
# seasonally adjusted price + seasonal component
# ================================================================

seasonal_adjustment_error <- max(
  abs(
    monthly_series$observed_price -
      (
        monthly_series$seasonally_adjusted_price +
          monthly_series$seasonal_component
      )
  ),

  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(seasonal_adjustment_error) ||
  seasonal_adjustment_error > 1e-10
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The seasonal-adjustment identity failed. ",
      "Maximum error: ",
      format(
        seasonal_adjustment_error,
        scientific = TRUE
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 14. VALIDATE THE FULL ADDITIVE DECOMPOSITION
#
# This validation applies only where the centered trend and
# remainder are available.
# ================================================================

complete_decomposition <- monthly_series |>
  filter(
    is.finite(trend_component),
    is.finite(remainder_component)
  )

reconstruction_error <- max(
  abs(
    complete_decomposition$observed_price -
      (
        complete_decomposition$trend_component +
          complete_decomposition$seasonal_component +
          complete_decomposition$remainder_component
      )
  ),

  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(reconstruction_error) ||
  reconstruction_error > 1e-8
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The full additive decomposition identity failed. ",
      "Maximum reconstruction error: ",
      format(
        reconstruction_error,
        scientific = TRUE
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 15. CALCULATE THE REMOVED SEASONAL ADJUSTMENT
#
# This is the vertical distance between observed and adjusted price:
#
# Y_t - Y_t^(SA) = S_t
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_series |>
  mutate(
    adjustment_direction = case_when(
      seasonal_component > 0 ~
        "Positive seasonal effect removed",

      seasonal_component < 0 ~
        "Negative seasonal effect removed",

      TRUE ~
        "No seasonal adjustment"
    ),

    absolute_seasonal_adjustment = abs(
      seasonal_component
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 16. IDENTIFY THE LARGEST SEASONAL ADJUSTMENTS
#
# The five largest adjustments are highlighted for teaching.
# ================================================================

n_highlight <- min(
  5L,
  nrow(monthly_series)
)

largest_adjustments <- monthly_series |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = absolute_seasonal_adjustment,

    n = n_highlight,

    with_ties = FALSE
  )

# ================================================================
# 17. SELECT ONE EXAMPLE OBSERVATION
#
# The latest occurrence of the month with the largest positive
# seasonal effect is used to illustrate the adjustment.
# ================================================================

largest_positive_month <- seasonal_indices |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = seasonal_effect,

    n = 1L,

    with_ties = FALSE
  ) |>
  pull(
    calendar_month_number
  )

example_adjustment <- monthly_series |>
  filter(
    calendar_month_number ==
      largest_positive_month
  ) |>
  slice_tail(
    n = 1L
  )

if (nrow(example_adjustment) == 0L) {

  stop(
    "The example seasonal adjustment could not be selected."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 18. DEFINE PRICE FORMATTING
# ================================================================

median_price <- median(
  monthly_series$observed_price,

  na.rm = TRUE
)

price_accuracy <- if (
  median_price >= 100
) {
  1
} else if (
  median_price >= 10
) {
  0.1
} else {
  0.01
}

price_formatter <- label_number(
  accuracy = price_accuracy,

  big.mark = ","
)

# ================================================================
# 19. CREATE THE EXAMPLE LABEL
# ================================================================

price_range <- diff(
  range(
    c(
      monthly_series$observed_price,
      monthly_series$seasonally_adjusted_price
    ),

    na.rm = TRUE
  )
)

if (
  !is.finite(price_range) ||
  price_range <= 0
) {

  price_range <- 1
}

example_label_y <- max(
  example_adjustment$observed_price,
  example_adjustment$seasonally_adjusted_price
) +
  0.12 * price_range

example_label <- paste0(
  format(
    example_adjustment$month,
    "%b %Y"
  ),
  "\n",
  "Observed: ",
  price_formatter(
    example_adjustment$observed_price
  ),
  "\n",
  "Seasonal effect: ",
  ifelse(
    example_adjustment$seasonal_component >= 0,
    "+",
    ""
  ),
  price_formatter(
    example_adjustment$seasonal_component
  ),
  "\n",
  "Adjusted: ",
  price_formatter(
    example_adjustment$seasonally_adjusted_price
  )
)

# ================================================================
# 20. CREATE THE SEASONALLY ADJUSTED PRICE FIGURE
# ================================================================

seasonally_adjusted_plot <- ggplot(
  data = monthly_series,

  aes(
    x = month
  )
) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Vertical segments show the seasonal adjustment:
  #
  # Observed - adjusted = seasonal component
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_segment(
    aes(
      x = month,

      xend = month,

      y = observed_price,

      yend = seasonally_adjusted_price,

      color = adjustment_direction
    ),

    linewidth = 0.65,

    alpha = 0.32
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Observed monthly adjusted price
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = observed_price,

      color = "Observed monthly price"
    ),

    linewidth = 0.65,

    alpha = 0.62,

    lineend = "round"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Seasonally adjusted price
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    aes(
      y = seasonally_adjusted_price,

      color = "Seasonally adjusted price"
    ),

    linewidth = 1.25,

    lineend = "round"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Observed monthly points
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    aes(
      y = observed_price
    ),

    color = "#94A3B8",

    size = 1.35,

    alpha = 0.48
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Highlight selected large seasonal adjustments
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = largest_adjustments,

    aes(
      x = month,

      y = seasonally_adjusted_price
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#D97706",

    fill = "white",

    shape = 21,

    size = 3.2,

    stroke = 1
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Highlight the illustrative adjustment
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_segment(
    data = example_adjustment,

    aes(
      x = month,

      xend = month,

      y = observed_price,

      yend = seasonally_adjusted_price
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#D97706",

    linewidth = 1.5,

    arrow = grid::arrow(
      length = grid::unit(
        0.13,
        "cm"
      ),

      type = "closed"
    )
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = example_adjustment,

    aes(
      x = month,

      y = observed_price
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#64748B",

    fill = "white",

    shape = 21,

    size = 3.8,

    stroke = 1.1
  ) +

  geom_point(
    data = example_adjustment,

    aes(
      x = month,

      y = seasonally_adjusted_price
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#059669",

    fill = "white",

    shape = 23,

    size = 4.2,

    stroke = 1.1
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Label the illustrative seasonal adjustment
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  annotate(
    geom = "label",

    x = example_adjustment$month,

    y = example_label_y,

    label = example_label,

    color = "#334155",

    fill = "white",

    fontface = "bold",

    size = 3,

    lineheight = 1,

    label.size = 0.3,

    label.padding = grid::unit(
      0.22,
      "lines"
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Controlled colors
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,

    values = c(
      "Observed monthly price" =
        "#94A3B8",

      "Seasonally adjusted price" =
        "#059669",

      "Positive seasonal effect removed" =
        "#2F6FA5",

      "Negative seasonal effect removed" =
        "#DC2626",

      "No seasonal adjustment" =
        "#64748B"
    ),

    breaks = c(
      "Observed monthly price",

    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Date axis
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 year",

    date_minor_breaks = "3 months",

    date_labels = "%Y",

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.01,

  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_y_continuous(

  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  labs(

    ),

# 21. DISPLAY THE FIGURE
```

## Time Series Decomposition


```{r}
# ================================================================
# REMAINDER COMPONENT OF MONTHLY ADJUSTED PRICES
# Classical additive decomposition
# ================================================================

library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(scales)

# ================================================================
# 1. VALIDATE THE INPUT DATASET
# ================================================================

if (!exists("monthly_data")) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The object 'monthly_data' does not exist. ",
      "Create the monthly adjusted-price dataset before ",
      "running this chunk."
    )
  )
}

required_columns <- c(
  "ticker",
  "month",
  "monthly_adjusted_price"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(
  required_columns,
  names(monthly_data)
)

if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The following required columns are missing from monthly_data: ",
      paste(
        missing_columns,
        collapse = ", "
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 2. SELECT THE FIRST VALID TICKER
# ================================================================

available_tickers <- monthly_data |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker)
  ) |>
  filter(
    !is.na(ticker),
    ticker != ""
  ) |>
  distinct(ticker) |>
  pull(ticker)

if (length(available_tickers) == 0L) {

  stop(
    "No valid ticker was found in monthly_data."
  )
}

ticker_selected <- available_tickers[1]

# ================================================================
# 3. PREPARE ONE ADJUSTED PRICE PER MONTH
#
# If duplicate ticker-month observations exist, the final finite
# price is retained.
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_data |>
  transmute(
    ticker = as.character(ticker),

    month = as.Date(month),

    monthly_adjusted_price = suppressWarnings(
      as.numeric(
        monthly_adjusted_price
      )
    )
  ) |>
  filter(
    ticker == ticker_selected,
    !is.na(month),
    is.finite(monthly_adjusted_price)
  ) |>
  arrange(month) |>
  group_by(
    ticker,
    month
  ) |>
  summarise(
    monthly_adjusted_price = last(
      monthly_adjusted_price
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(month)

n_months <- nrow(
  monthly_series
)

if (n_months < 24L) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "At least 24 monthly observations are required for an ",
      "annual classical decomposition. Only ",
      n_months,
      " were found for ",
      ticker_selected,
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 4. CHECK FOR DUPLICATED MONTHS
# ================================================================

duplicated_months <- monthly_series |>
  count(month) |>
  filter(
    n > 1L
  )

if (nrow(duplicated_months) > 0L) {

  stop(
    "The monthly price series contains duplicated months."
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 5. CHECK FOR MISSING CALENDAR MONTHS
#
# Classical decomposition requires a regularly spaced monthly
# series.
# ================================================================

expected_month_sequence <- seq.Date(
  from = min(
    monthly_series$month
  ),

  to = max(
    monthly_series$month
  ),

  by = "month"
)

missing_calendar_months <- expected_month_sequence[
  !expected_month_sequence %in%
    monthly_series$month
]

if (length(missing_calendar_months) > 0L) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The monthly series contains missing calendar months: ",
      paste(
        format(
          missing_calendar_months,
          "%b %Y"
        ),
        collapse = ", "
      ),
      ". Treat the missing months before applying classical ",
      "decomposition."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 6. CREATE THE MONTHLY TIME-SERIES OBJECT
#
# frequency = 12 defines the annual seasonal cycle.
# ================================================================

initial_year <- as.integer(
  format(
    min(monthly_series$month),
    "%Y"
  )
)

initial_month <- as.integer(
  format(
    min(monthly_series$month),
    "%m"
  )
)

monthly_price_ts <- stats::ts(
  data = monthly_series$monthly_adjusted_price,

  start = c(
    initial_year,
    initial_month
  ),

  frequency = 12
)

# ================================================================
# 7. APPLY CLASSICAL ADDITIVE DECOMPOSITION
#
# Y_t = T_t + S_t + R_t
#
# stats::decompose() estimates:
#
# - trend using a centered 2 x 12 moving average;
# - seasonality by averaging detrended prices by calendar month;
# - remainder by subtracting trend and seasonality.
# ================================================================

classical_decomposition <- stats::decompose(
  x = monthly_price_ts,

  type = "additive"
)

# ================================================================
# 8. EXTRACT THE COMPONENTS
# ================================================================

monthly_series <- monthly_series |>
  mutate(
    observed_price = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$x
    ),

    trend_component = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$trend
    ),

    seasonal_component = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$seasonal
    ),

    remainder_component = as.numeric(
      classical_decomposition$random
    ),

    seasonally_adjusted_price =
      observed_price -
      seasonal_component,

    detrended_price =
      observed_price -
      trend_component
  )

# ================================================================
# 9. RETAIN VALID REMAINDER OBSERVATIONS
#
# The first and final six months have no remainder because the
# centered 2 x 12 trend cannot be estimated at the sample edges.
# ================================================================

remainder_data <- monthly_series |>
  filter(
    is.finite(trend_component),
    is.finite(seasonal_component),
    is.finite(remainder_component)
  )

n_remainder_observations <- nrow(
  remainder_data
)

expected_remainder_observations <-
  n_months - 12L

if (
  n_remainder_observations !=
    expected_remainder_observations
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "Unexpected number of remainder observations. Expected ",
      expected_remainder_observations,
      " but obtained ",
      n_remainder_observations,
      "."
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 10. VALIDATE THE ADDITIVE DECOMPOSITION
#
# Y_t = T_t + S_t + R_t
# ================================================================

reconstruction_error <- max(
  abs(
    remainder_data$observed_price -
      (
        remainder_data$trend_component +
          remainder_data$seasonal_component +
          remainder_data$remainder_component
      )
  ),

  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(reconstruction_error) ||
  reconstruction_error > 1e-8
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The additive decomposition identity failed. ",
      "Maximum reconstruction error: ",
      format(
        reconstruction_error,
        scientific = TRUE
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 11. VALIDATE THE REMAINDER CALCULATION DIRECTLY
#
# R_t = Y_t - T_t - S_t
# ================================================================

manual_remainder <- with(
  remainder_data,

  observed_price -
    trend_component -
    seasonal_component
)

remainder_calculation_error <- max(
  abs(
    manual_remainder -
      remainder_data$remainder_component
  ),

  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(remainder_calculation_error) ||
  remainder_calculation_error > 1e-8
) {

  stop(
    paste0(
      "The manual remainder calculation does not match the ",
      "decomposition output. Maximum error: ",
      format(
        remainder_calculation_error,
        scientific = TRUE
      )
    )
  )
}

# ================================================================
# 12. CALCULATE ROBUST STANDARDIZED REMAINDERS
#
# Median and MAD are used to reduce the influence of large
# remainder observations when defining the reference scale.
# ================================================================

remainder_center <- median(
  remainder_data$remainder_component,

  na.rm = TRUE
)

remainder_scale <- mad(
  remainder_data$remainder_component,

  center = remainder_center,

  constant = 1.4826,

  na.rm = TRUE
)

# Fallback if MAD is zero or invalid

if (
  !is.finite(remainder_scale) ||
  remainder_scale <= 0
) {

  remainder_scale <- sd(
    remainder_data$remainder_component,

    na.rm = TRUE
  )
}

if (
  !is.finite(remainder_scale) ||
  remainder_scale <= 0
) {

  stop(
    "The remainder has no valid dispersion measure."
  )
}

remainder_data <- remainder_data |>
  mutate(
    robust_z_score =
      (
        remainder_component -
          remainder_center
      ) /
      remainder_scale,

    remainder_direction = case_when(
      remainder_component > 0 ~
        "Positive unexplained deviation",

      remainder_component < 0 ~
        "Negative unexplained deviation",

      TRUE ~
        "No unexplained deviation"
    ),

    remainder_class = case_when(
      abs(robust_z_score) > 3 ~
        "Highly unusual remainder",

      abs(robust_z_score) > 2 ~
        "Potentially unusual remainder",

      TRUE ~
        "Regular remainder"
    ),

    positive_remainder = if_else(
      remainder_component > 0,

      remainder_component,

      0
    ),

    negative_remainder = if_else(
      remainder_component < 0,

      remainder_component,

      0
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 13. SEPARATE REGULAR AND UNUSUAL REMAINDERS
#
# The threshold |robust z| > 2 is used for teaching emphasis.
# It is not presented as an automatic correction rule.
# ================================================================

regular_remainders <- remainder_data |>
  filter(
    abs(robust_z_score) <= 2
  )

unusual_remainders <- remainder_data |>
  filter(
    abs(robust_z_score) > 2
  )

highly_unusual_remainders <- remainder_data |>
  filter(
    abs(robust_z_score) > 3
  )

# ================================================================
# 14. SELECT THE LARGEST POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE REMAINDERS
# ================================================================

largest_positive_remainder <- remainder_data |>
  slice_max(
    order_by = remainder_component,

    n = 1L,

    with_ties = FALSE
  )

largest_negative_remainder <- remainder_data |>
  slice_min(
    order_by = remainder_component,

    n = 1L,

    with_ties = FALSE
  )

extreme_remainders <- bind_rows(
  largest_positive_remainder,
  largest_negative_remainder
) |>
  distinct(
    month,

    .keep_all = TRUE
  )

# ================================================================
# 15. DEFINE PRICE FORMATTING
#
# Remainders retain the original price unit.
# ================================================================

median_price <- median(
  remainder_data$observed_price,

  na.rm = TRUE
)

price_accuracy <- if (
  median_price >= 100
) {
  1
} else if (
  median_price >= 10
) {
  0.1
} else {
  0.01
}

price_formatter <- label_number(
  accuracy = price_accuracy,

  big.mark = ","
)

# ================================================================
# 16. CREATE LABELS FOR THE EXTREME REMAINDERS
# ================================================================

extreme_remainders <- extreme_remainders |>
  mutate(
    extreme_label = paste0(
      format(
        month,
        "%b %Y"
      ),
      "\n",
      "Remainder: ",
      if_else(
        remainder_component >= 0,
        "+",
        ""
      ),
      price_formatter(
        remainder_component
      ),
      "\n",
      "Robust z: ",
      number(
        robust_z_score,
        accuracy = 0.01
      )
    ),

    vertical_justification = if_else(
      remainder_component >= 0,

      -0.65,

      1.55
    )
  )

# ================================================================
# 17. DEFINE A SYMMETRIC VERTICAL SCALE
#
# Symmetric limits around zero make positive and negative
# unexplained deviations directly comparable.
# ================================================================

maximum_absolute_remainder <- max(
  abs(
    remainder_data$remainder_component
  ),

  na.rm = TRUE
)

if (
  !is.finite(maximum_absolute_remainder) ||
  maximum_absolute_remainder <= 0
) {

  maximum_absolute_remainder <- 1
}

vertical_limit <-
  1.28 *
  maximum_absolute_remainder

# ================================================================
# 18. DEFINE ROBUST REFERENCE THRESHOLDS
#
# These horizontal lines correspond to:
#
# median remainder ± 2 × robust scale
# ================================================================

upper_reference <- remainder_center +
  2 * remainder_scale

lower_reference <- remainder_center -
  2 * remainder_scale

# ================================================================
# 19. CREATE THE REMAINDER FIGURE
# ================================================================

remainder_component_plot <- ggplot(
  data = remainder_data,

  aes(
    x = month,
    y = remainder_component
  )
) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Positive remainder area
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = 0,

      ymax = positive_remainder
    ),

    fill = "#2F6FA5",

    alpha = 0.15
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Negative remainder area
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = negative_remainder,

      ymax = 0
    ),

    fill = "#DC2626",

    alpha = 0.15
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Robust reference band
  #
  # This band shows the interval:
  #
  # median remainder ± 2 × MAD-based scale
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = -Inf,

      xmax = Inf,

      ymin = lower_reference,

      ymax = upper_reference
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    fill = "#64748B",

    alpha = 0.06
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Robust threshold lines
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = upper_reference,

    color = "#D97706",

    linewidth = 0.55,

    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = lower_reference,

    color = "#D97706",

    linewidth = 0.55,

    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Zero reference
  #
  # R_t = 0 means that the observed price is completely explained
  # by the estimated trend and seasonal components.
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,

    color = "#334155",

    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Complete remainder series
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_line(
    color = "#64748B",

    linewidth = 0.72,

    alpha = 0.82,

    lineend = "round"
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Regular remainder observations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = regular_remainders,

    aes(
      x = month,
      y = remainder_component,
      color = remainder_direction
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    size = 2,

    alpha = 0.65
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Potentially unusual remainder observations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = unusual_remainders,

    aes(
      x = month,
      y = remainder_component
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#D97706",

    fill = "white",

    shape = 21,

    size = 3.5,

    stroke = 1.05
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Highly unusual remainder observations
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_point(
    data = highly_unusual_remainders,

    aes(
      x = month,
      y = remainder_component
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#991B1B",

    fill = "#FEE2E2",

    shape = 21,

    size = 4.2,

    stroke = 1.25
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Label the largest positive and negative remainders
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  geom_text(
    data = extreme_remainders,

    aes(
      x = month,

      y = remainder_component,

      label = extreme_label,

      vjust = vertical_justification
    ),

    inherit.aes = FALSE,

    color = "#334155",

    size = 2.9,

    fontface = "bold",

    lineheight = 0.95,

    check_overlap = TRUE
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Point colors
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_color_manual(
    name = NULL,

    values = c(
      "Positive unexplained deviation" =
        "#2F6FA5",

      "Negative unexplained deviation" =
        "#DC2626",

      "No unexplained deviation" =
        "#059669"
    ),

    breaks = c(
      "Positive unexplained deviation",
      "Negative unexplained deviation",
      "No unexplained deviation"
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Date axis
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_x_date(
    date_breaks = "1 year",

    date_minor_breaks = "3 months",

    date_labels = "%Y",

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0.01,
        0.02
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Symmetric remainder scale
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(
      -vertical_limit,
      vertical_limit
    ),

    labels = price_formatter,

    breaks = pretty_breaks(
      n = 5
    ),

    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(
        0,
        0
      )
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Titles and labels
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  labs(
    title =
      "What Remains After Removing Trend and Seasonality?",

    subtitle = paste0(
      ticker_selected,
      " monthly adjusted prices | ",
      "R(t) = Y(t) − T(t) − S(t)"
    ),

    x = "Month",

    y = expression(
      hat(R)[t]
    ),

    caption = paste0(
      "Blue values represent positive unexplained deviations; ",
      "red values represent negative unexplained deviations. ",
      "Orange circles have |robust z-score| > 2, and dark-red ",
      "circles have |robust z-score| > 3. ",
      "The dashed lines show the median remainder ± 2 robust scales."
    )
  ) +

  # --------------------------------------------------------------
  # Presentation theme
  # --------------------------------------------------------------

  theme_minimal(
    base_size = 13
  ) +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(
      size = 20,

      face = "bold",

      color = "#172033",

      margin = margin(
        b = 4
      )
    ),

    plot.subtitle = element_text(
      size = 11.5,

      color = "#475569",

      margin = margin(
        b = 13
      )
    ),

    plot.caption = element_text(
      size = 8.5,

      color = "#64748B",

      hjust = 0,

      lineheight = 1.15,

      margin = margin(
        t = 10
      )
    ),

    axis.title = element_text(
      size = 11,

      face = "bold",

      color = "#334155"
    ),

    axis.text = element_text(
      size = 8.5,

      color = "#64748B"
    ),

    panel.grid.major = element_line(
      color = "#E5E7EB",

      linewidth = 0.4
    ),

    panel.grid.minor.x = element_line(
      color = "#F1F5F9",

      linewidth = 0.25
    ),

    panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),

    legend.position = "bottom",

    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 9.5,

      color = "#475569"
    ),

    legend.key.width = grid::unit(
      0.9,
      "cm"
    ),

    plot.margin = margin(
      t = 10,

      r = 20,

      b = 8,

      l = 10
    )
  ) +

  guides(
    color = guide_legend(
      override.aes = list(
        size = 3,

        alpha = 0.9
      )
    )
  )

remainder_component_plot
```


## Time Series Features

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Trend strength

Trend strength compares the remainder with the
**trend component**:

$$
F_T =
\max\left(
0,\,
1 -
\frac{\operatorname{Var}(R_t)}
     {\operatorname{Var}(T_t + R_t)}
\right).
$$

- $F_T \approx 0$: little or no trend
- $F_T \approx 1$: strong trend

:::

::: {.column width="50%"}

### Seasonal strength

Seasonal strength compares the remainder with the
**detrended series**:

$$
F_S =
\max\left(
0,\,
1 -
\frac{\operatorname{Var}(R_t)}
     {\operatorname{Var}(S_t + R_t)}
\right)
$$

- $F_S \approx 0$: little or no seasonality
- $F_S \approx 1$: strong seasonality

:::

::::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
Both measures range from **0 to 1**. Values closer to 1 indicate that
the corresponding systematic component explains substantially more
variation than the remainder.
:::
